label: S0315
statement: LEMMA (G=0 pointer lemma). Fix a streaming system with q_0 a constant tuple and q_{t+1} = F_t(q_t, p_{t+1}), where every output coordinate of every F_t is a literal of (q_1..q_S, b) or a constant (gate-free, G=0). Suppose the codes q_t(p) are pairwise distinct over the live prefixes P_t (prefixes of members of F). Let d_t be the least size of a coordinate set I subset [t] such that p -> p|I is injective on P_t. Then S >= d_t, and hence S >= log2 |P_t|. Proof: by induction on t, each coordinate of q_t, as a function of p in {0,1}^t, is a constant or +/- p_i for a single i <= t. Base: q_0 is constant. Step: a coordinate of q_{t+1} is a constant, the literal p_{t+1} or its negation, or a literal of some q_{t,k}, which by hypothesis is a constant or +/- p_i. So the claim holds at t+1. Let I_t be the set of indices i used by some coordinate; |I_t| <= S, and q_t(p) is a function of p|I_t. If p, p' in P_t agree on I_t then q_t(p) = q_t(p'), so p = p' by injectivity. Hence p -> p|I_t is injective on P_t, giving d_t <= |I_t| <= S. Scope: exact for gate-free systems at any n and S, with injective live codes; it says nothing about gates (G >= 1), decoder size or dead codes.

label: S0318
statement: statement: For the full truth-table family F={0,1}^{2^n}, every streaming search system whose state at time t separates distinct live prefixes must have S_t≥t bits; moreover the bound is attained with zero update gates by storing the input prefix verbatim. Proof: every length-t string p has a completion to a member of F, so there are exactly 2^t live prefixes. Pairwise distinct live codes require at least 2^t state values, hence S_t≥log2(2^t)=t. For attainment, initialize q_0 empty and at each step wire the incoming bit into a fresh state coordinate, retaining all earlier coordinates unchanged; all transitions are wires, so G=0, and q_t=p. The decoder reconstructs the truth table from q_{2^n}. This is exact for the full-family search model and shows that a zero-gate optimum can arise solely from state width equal to the prefix length; it gives no nontrivial bound when S_t<t.

label: S0319
statement: statement: Residual-set state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N recognized by a deterministic streaming system with state q_t(p) after prefix p of length t, deterministic transitions, and a final decoder that accepts exactly members of F. For each length-t prefix p define R_p={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. Then the number of distinct states at time t is at least the number of distinct sets R_p. Proof: if R_p and R_p' differ, choose u in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pu and p'u is in F. If q_t(p)=q_t(p'), determinism implies that processing the common suffix u produces the same final state, so the decoder gives the same acceptance answer on both strings, contradiction. Therefore prefixes with distinct residual sets have distinct states; selecting one prefix for each distinct residual set gives the bound. This only forces pairwise separation when residual sets differ, and permits merging prefixes with identical residual sets.

label: S0320
statement: statement: Residual-set quotient lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For every t<N and bit b, R_{t+1}(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R_t(p)}. Consequently, identifying prefixes with equal residual sets gives a deterministic quotient transition on the reachable classes: [p]_t --b--> [pb]_{t+1}; this is well-defined because equal R_t(p),R_t(p') imply equal restrictions by first bit b, hence equal R_{t+1}(pb),R_{t+1}(p'b). Proof: for each suffix v, v belongs to the left set iff pbv is in F, iff bv is in R_t(p); the well-definedness follows by applying this equivalence to both prefixes. The quotient exactly recognizes F with final acceptance determined by whether the residual set at t=N contains the empty string. It has exactly the number of distinct residual sets at each level, a lower bound on states for any deterministic decision transducer. This is a decision-language construction; it does not satisfy the stronger SEARCH requirement that all distinct live prefixes have distinct states, and gives no gate-cost or decoder-size bound.

statement: statement: Live/dead state-count bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, let P_t be the set of live length-t prefixes, and let L_t=|P_t|. In a streaming system with S state bits that assigns pairwise distinct states to live prefixes and gives every dead prefix a state outside the set of live-prefix states, if at least one dead prefix exists then 2^S >= L_t+1, hence S >= ceil(log2(L_t+1)); if no dead prefix exists then 2^S >= L_t. Proof: the L_t live prefixes require L_t distinct elements of the state set. A dead prefix, when one exists, requires a further element outside those L_t states. The state set has cardinality exactly 2^S, proving the inequalities. Conversely, as a pure assignment of codes, L_t codes suffice when there are no dead prefixes and L_t+1 codes suffice when there are dead prefixes, by assigning distinct codes to the live prefixes and one remaining code to all dead prefixes. This is only a state-count statement; it asserts no realizability or bound for transition-circuit gate cost.

This is only a state-count statement; it asserts no realizability or bound for transition-circuit gate cost.

label: S0322
statement:
statement: LEMMA-A-REPAIR (corrected). Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N. A streaming search system has initial state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t, x_{t+1}) where q_t(p) depends only on the length-t prefix p, and a decoder D on the final state q_N(w) which, for every w in {0,1}^N, outputs a circuit computing w if w in F and rejects otherwise. Call a length-t prefix p LIVE if there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F, DEAD otherwise. For a live prefix p define its residual set R_t(p) = {u in {0,1}^{N-t} : pu in F}. For a dead prefix, R_t(p) = empty set.

Claim: In any such system that correctly decides membership in F, the states at time t must satisfy:
(1) Live/dead separation: if p is live and p' is dead then q_t(p) != q_t(p').
(2) Residual distinction: if p, p' are live and R_t(p) != R_t(p') then q_t(p) != q_t(p').
(3) Merging permitted: if R_t(p) = R_t(p') then q_t(p) may equal q_t(p').

Consequently, the number of distinct states reachable at time t is at least D_t + [exists dead prefix], where D_t is the number of distinct non-empty residual sets among length-t prefixes.

Proof: (1) Suppose p live, p' dead, but q_t(p) = q_t(p'). Since p is live, there exists u with pu in F. Since p' is dead, p'u not in F. Processing the common suffix u from the same state q_t(p)=q_t(p') yields the same final state by determinism, so the decoder gives the same answer on pu and p'u, contradicting that pu in F and p'u not in F.
(2) Suppose p, p' live with R_t(p) != R_t(p'). Then there exists u in the symmetric difference. Exactly one of pu, p'u is in F. If q_t(p)=q_t(p'), determinism gives the same final state on suffix u, so the decoder gives the same answer, contradiction.
(3) If R_t(p)=R_t(p'), then for every suffix u, pu in F iff p'u in F. Merging q_t(p)=q_t(p') preserves correctness because all future suffixes lead to identical acceptance outcomes. The lower bound on state count follows by picking one representative for each distinct non-empty residual set (giving D_t states) and, if any dead prefix exists, one additional state for all dead prefixes (since they all have R_t=empty and can share a state by (3)).

label: S0326
statement:
statement: Residual-partition characterization for deterministic membership streaming: at every cut t, equal machine states imply equal residual subsets R_t(p)={u:pu∈F}; conversely the residual subsets themselves form a sufficient deterministic state representation, with transition on bit b given by R↦{v:bv∈R}.
proof: Let p and q be length-t prefixes whose machine states agree. For an arbitrary suffix u of length N−t, applying the same deterministic transitions to the same suffix from equal states yields equal final states. The decoder therefore gives the same membership answer for pu and qu. As this holds for every u, their residual subsets are equal. Conversely, define the state associated with prefix p to be R_t(p). On reading b, the next residual is exactly {v : bv∈R_t(p)}, which equals R_{t+1}(pb) by definition. At t=N, the residual is {ε} exactly for members and empty exactly for nonmembers, so the decoder accepts precisely members. This proves sufficiency and the claimed transition rule.

structure.gap: The residual partition characterizes membership state requirements but does not determine the minimum per-step update circuit cost G_max, nor the joint Pareto frontier at fixed S<N and decoder cost D for SC_{3,1}, SC_{3,2}, or affine families.
structure.lemma: For any deterministic one-pass membership transducer on a finite family F of N-bit strings, states at cut t induce a partition of the length-t prefixes that refines equality of acceptance residuals: if two prefixes reach the same state, their residual subsets of {0,1}^{N-t} are equal. Proof: fix prefixes p,q reaching the same state. For every suffix u, determinism gives the same final state after processing u from that shared state, so the decoder returns the same membership bit on pu and qu. Thus pu∈F iff qu∈F for every u, exactly R_t(p)=R_t(q). Conversely, assigning one state per distinct residual (including the empty residual if present) is sufficient for membership provided transitions map each residual R on next bit b to R_b={v: bv∈R}, with unreachable/empty states handled by the empty residual. This is a finite-state characterization and says nothing about circuit gate cost.

label: S0329
statement:
statement_start: Residual-state circuit upper bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, with N finite, and let D_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} as p ranges over length-t prefixes. If each residual set is encoded injectively by S_t bits, then the induced transition on reachable encoded states is realizable by a Boolean circuit with at most 2^{S_t+1}(2S_t+4)S_{t+1} NOT/AND/OR gates, when behavior off the reachable domain is arbitrary.
proof: Put k=S_t+1. Define a total transition function on all k-bit inputs by using the residual derivative {v:bv in R} when the state bits encode a reachable residual R, and outputting 0^{S_{t+1}} otherwise. For each output coordinate, its truth table has at most 2^k satisfying assignments. Write its disjunctive normal form: each minterm uses at most k NOT gates and k-1 binary AND gates; combining at most 2^k minterms uses at most 2^k-1 binary OR gates. Thus at most 2^k(2k) gates per output coordinate suffice, which is bounded by 2^k(2S_t+4). Multiply by S_{t+1}. On reachable transitions, correctness follows from R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv in R_t(p)}.

label: S0330
statement:
statement_start: One-hot residual transition lemma. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual suffix sets, including the empty set if it occurs, and let D_t=|R_t|. Encode each residual by its own one-hot state bit. For each input bit b, the next residual is δ_b(R)={v:bv∈R}. The transition from cut t to t+1 can be implemented with at most 2D_tD_{t+1}+D_{t+1} NOT/AND/OR gates, with arbitrary behavior on invalid one-hot states.
proof: For each next residual T∈R_{t+1}, define its output bit as the OR of terms (z_R AND [b=0]) over all R∈R_t with δ_0(R)=T, together with terms (z_R AND [b=1]) over all R∈R_t with δ_1(R)=T. Here z_R is the one-hot bit for R. Implement [b=0] with one NOT gate and [b=1] by the input wire. Each term uses at most one AND gate, and there are at most 2D_t terms per output. Combining k terms uses at most k−1 OR gates; allowing an empty disjunction as constant 0, each output costs at most 2D_t AND gates plus 2D_t OR gates. Across D_{t+1} outputs this costs at most 4D_tD_{t+1} gates, plus at most one shared NOT gate. Thus the stated 2D_tD_{t+1}+D_{t+1} bound is not justified by this construction; the proved bound is 4D_tD_{t+1}+1. For a reachable one-hot state z_R, exactly one z_R is 1, and exactly the output for δ_b(R) evaluates to 1, so the transition is correct.

label: S0333
statement:
statement: Common-accepting-suffix separation for full-search streaming. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, and let a deterministic streaming system read an N-bit word and end in a state from which a decoder outputs a circuit computing that word whenever the word belongs to F. Fix a cut t. If distinct length-t prefixes p and q have a common suffix u with pu, qu in F, then the states reached after p and q are distinct. Proof: if those states were equal, determinism implies that appending the same u reaches the same final state. The decoder would therefore output the same circuit C on both inputs. Correctness requires C to compute pu and also qu. Since p != q, pu != qu, and a single Boolean circuit computes only one truth table, a contradiction. This establishes separation only for live prefixes with intersecting accepting-suffix sets; it makes no claim for live prefixes whose accepting-suffix sets are disjoint, nor does it bound transition-circuit gate cost.
proof: Assume the states after p and q are equal. Applying identical deterministic transitions for each bit of u preserves equality, so the final states after pu and qu are equal. The decoder returns the same circuit on both. Since pu and qu are members of F, correctness requires that circuit to compute both truth tables. They differ because p and q differ, contradiction.

label: S0334
statement:
statement: For the explicitly defined family F of truth tables of constants, literals, and one binary Boolean operation applied to any pair of the three input variables in deterministic truth-table order, at cut t=7 there is a set P of 19 distinct live prefixes such that every two distinct p,q in P have a common suffix u with pu,qu in F. Consequently every deterministic full-search streaming system whose final decoder outputs a correct circuit for every member of F has at least 19 distinct states at cut 7. Proof: by the asserted pairwise common-suffix property, for each distinct p,q choose u with pu,qu in F. If their states were equal, determinism would give equal final states after the same u; the decoder would output one circuit for both distinct truth tables, contradicting correctness. Thus all 19 states are distinct.
proof: The family and witness are finite and explicitly enumerated in experiment cm-4fee8db16c8d462d; the corrected follow-up computation outputs all 19 witness prefixes and checks a common accepting suffix for each of the 171 pairs. For each pair, equality of states propagates under the common suffix by determinism. At the end the same decoder output would have to compute two different words pu and qu, impossible. Hence the 19 prefixes occupy distinct states.

label: S0335
statement:
statement: Common-suffix clique state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut t. Form a graph whose vertices are the live length-t prefixes p (those with at least one suffix u such that pu is in F), joining distinct p,q when they share an accepting suffix: there exists u with pu, qu in F. Every deterministic full-search streaming machine that ends in a decoder outputting the input truth table on each member of F uses at least omega(G_t) distinct states after t bits, where omega is the graph clique number.
proof: Take any clique C in G_t. For distinct p,q in C, choose a shared accepting suffix u. If the machine had the same state after p and q, determinism would make the final states after pu and qu equal, so the decoder would output the same circuit for both. But pu and qu are distinct truth tables, contradicting full-search correctness. Thus all prefixes in C occupy pairwise distinct states, requiring at least |C| states. Maximize over cliques C to obtain at least omega(G_t) states.
scope: All finite N, all F subset {0,1}^N, every cut t; constrains states only and gives no transition-gate lower bound.

label: S0336
statement: statement: Finite state-capacity bound at the SC_{3,1} middle cut. Let F be the specified family of 38 truth tables, let t=7, and let P_t be its live prefixes. Any streaming encoding that assigns distinct S-bit states to live prefixes and a state disjoint from those states to at least one dead prefix must have S>=6. Proof: The 38 members of F have distinct length-7 prefixes: there are only 2^(8-7)=2 possible suffixes per prefix, so at most two distinct truth tables can share a prefix; more directly, the corrected prefix enumeration for this family gives |P_7|=38. Injectivity therefore requires 38 distinct states for live prefixes. The required dead-prefix state is outside those 38, so 2^S>=39. Since 2^5=32<39<=64=2^6, S>=6. This bound is tight as a state-capacity count alone: 64 available codes can hold the 38 live prefixes and at least one dead code. It gives no transition-circuit gate bound and does not determine G_max.

statement: statement: For every N-bit input stream language L subseteq {0,1}^N, an exact one-pass transducer with S=N state bits can update the state using zero non-constant gates per step (basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants; free wires), by storing the raw prefix in the first t coordinates and zeroing the remaining coordinates; a decoder decides L from the final state.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and induction: initialize q=0^N. At step t+1 copy the input bit into coordinate t+1 and wire earlier coordinates unchanged; unused coordinates remain zero. Thus after N steps q equals the entire stream, so the decoder computes its membership in L. Cost is zero because all transition outputs are wires or constants. This proves the spec's trivial S=N upper bound only; it gives no result for S<N and no lower bound on G_max.

statement: statement: Overlap-graph coloring lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut t. Form a graph H_t on the live length-t prefixes, joining distinct p,q iff some suffix u of length N-t has pu,qu in F. In any deterministic streaming system whose decoder outputs the truth table on every member of F, the states at cut t form a proper coloring of H_t. Thus there are at least chi(H_t) states and at least ceil(log2 chi(H_t)) state bits. Proof: if adjacent p,q had the same state, processing their shared suffix u would lead to the same final state and decoder output. But pu and qu are distinct members of F, so that output cannot be correct for both. Hence adjacent vertices have distinct states, and the state map is a proper coloring.

label: S0340
statement:
statement: Explicit C5 separation for overlap bounds. There is an F subset {0,1}^6 at cut t=3 whose common-accepting-suffix graph is C5, so the chromatic lower bound requires 3 states while the clique lower bound requires only 2. Choose distinct 3-bit prefixes p_0,...,p_4 and suffixes u_0,...,u_4, and set F={p_i u_i,p_i u_{i+1 mod 5}:0<=i<5}. Each prefix has accepting-suffix set {u_i,u_{i+1}}, so intersections occur exactly for neighbors on C5. C5 has clique number 2 and chromatic number 3: it is triangle-free and an odd cycle, and a 3-coloring exists.
proof: For distinct i,k, {u_i,u_{i+1}} intersects {u_k,u_{k+1}} exactly when i,k are consecutive modulo 5. Thus the graph is C5. A triangle-free graph has clique number at most 2, and C5 has edges, so omega=2. An odd cycle is not 2-colorable; assigning colors A,B,A,B,C around its five vertices is a proper 3-coloring. The previously proved overlap-state argument makes the machine's state assignment a proper coloring.

label: S0341
statement: statement: Residual machine finite upper bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and Q_t={R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}. Then |Q_t|<=min(2^t,2^(2^(N-t))). The deterministic transition delta_t(R,b)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R} maps Q_t into Q_{t+1} and recognizes F by accepting at t=N exactly when R_N={epsilon}. Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, so the image Q_t has size at most 2^t. Every residual is a subset of the 2^(N-t) suffixes, so there are at most 2^(2^(N-t)) possible residuals. For R=R_t(p), v belongs to delta_t(R,b) iff bv belongs to R iff pbv belongs to F iff v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb), hence delta_t(R,b)=R_{t+1}(pb) and lies in Q_{t+1}. At t=N, R_N(p) contains epsilon iff p belongs to F; since its universe is {epsilon}, the stated decoder is exact. This gives an explicit finite-state upper bound; it asserts no bound on Boolean gate complexity of delta_t.

statement: statement: Sparse-domain transition-circuit upper bound. Let k,q,r be nonnegative integers, with k>=1. Let D be any subset of {0,1}^k of size r, and let h:D->{0,1}^q be any prescribed map. In the basis NOT, binary AND, binary OR, and constants, there is a q-output Boolean circuit agreeing with h on D and using at most k+r(k-1)+q max(r-1,0) non-constant gates; its behavior outside D is unrestricted. Proof: Create the k input literals x_i and ¬x_i using at most k NOT gates. For each a in D, form its equality indicator e_a=AND_{i=1}^k l_{a,i}, where l_{a,i}=x_i if a_i=1 and ¬x_i otherwise. This uses k-1 binary AND gates per a. For output coordinate j, form the OR of e_a over those a for which h(a)_j=1. If there are d_j such rows, this needs at most max(d_j-1,0) OR gates, at most max(r-1,0). For any z in D, exactly e_z is 1 among all row indicators, so the jth output equals h(z)_j. Summing the costs gives the stated bound. If an output has no selected rows, use constant 0. This is an upper bound for an arbitrary prescribed partial transition table; it does not assert a lower bound or an exact G_max.

statement: statement: DNF transition upper bound with shared literals. Let k,q be integers with k>=1 and q>=1. Every function f:{0,1}^k->{0,1}^q has a NOT/AND/OR circuit of size at most q(2^k(k+1)+1), with binary AND/OR gates, shared input negations, and zero-cost constant outputs. Proof: For an output true on r input rows, use the OR of those r minterms. The input negations cost at most k gates total and each minterm uses k-1 AND gates; combining r terms uses r-1 OR gates. In a circuit convention without free constants, constant outputs require separate treatment.

label: S0345
statement: statement: Conflict-graph state lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a set of distinct N-bit truth tables. At cut t, let P_t be the length-t prefixes of members of F, and form H_t on P_t by joining distinct p,q when some suffix u has pu,qu in F. In any deterministic streaming system whose final decoder outputs a circuit computing its input word for every member of F, adjacent prefixes reach distinct states. Therefore the state assignment is a proper coloring of H_t, so the system has at least chi(H_t) states at cut t and at least ceil(log2 chi(H_t)) state bits. Proof: suppose adjacent p,q reach the same state, and choose a common accepting suffix u. Determinism makes the final states after pu and qu equal, so the decoder outputs the same circuit on both. Correctness requires that circuit to compute both distinct truth tables, which is impossible. Thus adjacent vertices have different states. A proper coloring of H_t needs at least chi(H_t) colors, and S bits encode at most 2^S states, giving 2^S >= chi(H_t). This bounds state count only; it does not bound transition-circuit gate cost.

label: S0347
statement: statement: Decoder-capacity lower bound (conditional on D being decoder-output bits). Let F be a finite set of M distinct truth tables, and suppose a deterministic full-search streaming machine has a decoder whose output is encoded by D bits and identifies the exact truth table f on every f in F. Then D >= ceil(log2 M). Proof: correctness requires distinct decoder outputs for distinct truth tables, since one output cannot identify two different truth tables. Thus the decoder takes at least M distinct values on reachable final states. Its D-bit output has at most 2^D values, so 2^D >= M and D >= ceil(log2 M). The argument is independent of transition encoding and update-circuit cost. It constrains a fixed (S,G_max,D) frame only when D counts bits that bound the number of distinguishable decoded truth tables; it does not establish an optimal Pareto point.

label: S0349
statement:
statement: Per-cut conflict-graph characterization of full-search state assignments. Fix a finite family F subset {0,1}^N and a cut t. Let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F}. Form the graph H_t on P_t, joining distinct p,q exactly when there is a suffix u with pu and qu both in F. Any deterministic streaming system whose final decoder returns the input truth table on every member of F assigns different states to adjacent vertices of H_t. Consequently its number of states is at least chi(H_t), and at least chi(H_t)+1 if it must also assign every dead prefix a state outside the live-prefix states. Conversely, any proper coloring of H_t gives a per-cut state assignment satisfying all same-suffix output-distinguishability constraints; this converse is only a per-cut assignment and asserts no compatible transition circuits across cuts.
proof: For an edge {p,q}, choose a suffix u witnessing the edge. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would take that common state to the same final state after reading u. The decoder would return one truth table for both pu and qu, contrary to correctness because p≠q implies pu≠qu. Thus every edge has differently colored endpoints under the machine's state map, so its image is a proper coloring and has at least chi(H_t) colors. Under the additional live/dead-separation rule, a dead prefix must use a state not used by any live prefix, adding one state. Conversely, a proper coloring separates every edge by definition, which is exactly the listed pairwise same-suffix constraint. This does not establish that the colorings at different cuts are linked by a realizable update circuit.

statement: statement: Residual doubling lemma. Let N>=1, F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and for 0<=t<=N let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, with D_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Then for every 0<=t<N, D_(t+1)<=2D_t. Proof: for p of length t and b in {0,1}, R_(t+1)(pb)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: (b,v) in R_t(p)}. Thus the residual after extending p by b is a function only of (R_t(p),b). There are D_t possible residuals at level t and two choices of b, so at most 2D_t next residuals. Taking the image cannot increase this count. This bounds the size of the canonical residual representation only; it asserts no transition-circuit gate-cost bound.

statement:
statement: Residual-index transition lemma. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}, with D_t=|R_t|. Then D_{t+1}<=2D_t. Moreover, choose any injective index encoding e_t:R_t->{0,1}^{s_t} and e_{t+1}:R_{t+1}->{0,1}^{s_{t+1}}, where s_i=ceil(log2 D_i). For each residual R and next bit b, define delta(R,b)={v:bv in R}. This belongs to R_{t+1}; hence the transition from the encoded pair (e_t(R),b) to e_{t+1}(delta(R,b)) is well-defined. There exists a Boolean circuit using NOT, binary AND, and binary OR with at most D_t(2s_t+1)(2s_{t+1}+1) gates implementing this transition on all reachable encoded pairs; its behavior elsewhere may be arbitrary.
Proof. For each R in R_t and b in {0,1}, delta(R,b) is the residual after extending any prefix p realizing R by b, so it is in R_{t+1}. Thus R_{t+1} is contained in the set of at most 2D_t such derivatives. For the circuit, for each of the at most 2D_t reachable input codes z=(e_t(R),b), form an equality indicator h_z as the conjunction of the s_t+1 input literals; this uses at most 2(s_t+1)-1 gates (NOT literals can be shared once across all z). Each output bit is the OR of those h_z whose prescribed next-code bit is 1. Combining across output coordinates, use at most 2D_t(s_t+1) AND gates for the indicators and at most 2D_t s_{t+1} OR gates; input negations cost at most s_t+1 shared NOT gates. This total is at most D_t(2s_t+1)(2s_{t+1}+1), since s_t,s_{t+1}>=0 and the right side dominates the displayed sum. The indicators are one-hot on the reachable input pairs because the encodings are injective. Therefore each output bit equals the prescribed next-code bit there. If D_t=0, no reachable states exist and the zero-output circuit suffices.

statement:
statement: Residuals exactly characterize minimum membership states. For F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t, let R_t(p)={u:pu in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let D_t be the number of distinct residuals. Every deterministic one-pass machine deciding F has at least D_t states after t bits. Conversely, a layered machine can decide F using exactly D_i states at each cut i.
proof: If two prefixes with distinct residuals reach the same state, some suffix u belongs to exactly one residual. Reading u from the common state gives the same final answer, contradicting exact membership. Thus at least D_t states are necessary. For sufficiency, use the realized residuals as states at each cut i. On bit b, transition R to {v:bv in R}; if R=R_i(p), this equals R_{i+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined. At cut N, accept the residual {epsilon} and reject the empty residual. The construction has exactly D_i states at each cut and decides F.

statement:
statement: Gate-free coordinate-projection lemma. Let a deterministic streaming machine use zero non-constant update gates in the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}, with state q_t in {0,1}^S and input bits x_1,...,x_N read in order. For every cut t, each state coordinate is either a constant or equal to one of x_1,...,x_t. Hence the state map at cut t is a coordinate projection with possible duplicated or constant coordinates. If the machine is correct for full search on a family F, that projection must be injective on the live prefixes P_t={p: exists u, pu in F}.
proof: At cut 0 the state is fixed, so every coordinate is constant. Assume the assertion holds at cut t. With zero non-constant gates, each coordinate of q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) is either a wire from a coordinate of q_t, a wire from x_{t+1}, or a constant. By the induction hypothesis, each resulting coordinate is therefore constant or one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. This proves the coordinate description for every cut. For injectivity, suppose distinct live prefixes p and q at cut t had the same state. Choose any suffix u with pu in F. Determinism gives the same final state after reading u from either prefix state. Full-search correctness would require the decoder to return pu on input pu and qu on input qu whenever both are members; more generally, choosing a suffix that completes both when one exists contradicts distinct outputs. In particular, the conclusion as stated requires the full-search model’s live-prefix state-separation condition: under that condition distinct live prefixes must have distinct states. Thus the projection is injective on P_t.

statement: One-hot residual transition upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0 <= t < N, let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} over all prefixes p of length t, and let d_t=|R_t|; define R_{t+1}, d_{t+1} analogously. There is an exact transition from one-hot encodings of R_t to one-hot encodings of R_{t+1}, on every reachable residual state and input bit b, realizable with at most 2d_t+3d_{t+1}+1 gates in the {AND, OR, NOT} basis, with shared fan-out free. statement: Constructive one-hot implementation bound. Let Q be a set of d>=1 states and delta:Q×{0,1}->Q be any deterministic transition map. Let r=|im(delta)|. Under the one-hot encoding with one state-indicator input per state and a Boolean input bit x, delta is implemented on valid one-hot inputs by a fan-in-two circuit with at most 4d-r+1 gates, counting one shared NOT gate for x. Proof: For each source i and input b create the term q_i AND x when b=1 and q_i AND (NOT x) when b=0. This uses 2d AND gates and one shared NOT. For each destination j in im(delta), OR together its k_j incoming terms using k_j-1 binary OR gates. Since sum_j k_j=2d and there are r nonempty destinations, the OR count is 2d-r. Thus total is 4d-r+1. For a valid one-hot input with q_i=1 and input x=b, exactly the term indexed (i,b) is true, so exactly the destination delta(i,b) is asserted. This is an upper bound for this explicit circuit construction only; it does not prove minimal G_max or a lower bound for Lemma M.

statement: statement: Residual-transition upper bound (general finite-family lemma). Let N>=1 and F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let D_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). Then D_{t+1}<=2D_t for every t<N. Moreover, there exist canonical per-cut states indexed by distinct residuals such that reading bit b maps state R in level t to the residual R_b={v: bv in R} at level t+1; this transition is well-defined and exact. Proof: If p,q have the same residual R_t(p)=R_t(q)=R, then for either bit b, R_{t+1}(pb)={v:bv in R}={v:bv in R_{t+1}(qb)}, so the child residual depends only on (R,b), not on the chosen prefix. Each residual has at most two children, one for each b; hence there are at most 2D_t distinct child residuals. Assign one state per residual and use this child map for transitions. At t=N, the residual is either {epsilon} (if p in F) or empty, so this automaton decides membership in F. Scope: state count at cut t is D_t and the update is an abstract transition on residual labels; this proves no bound on Boolean gate cost under any fixed bit encoding, no full-search witness decoding result, and no Lemma M Pareto point.

statement: statement: Full-search state-capacity lemma and SC_{3,1} consequence. Let F be a family of M distinct N-bit truth tables. At cut t let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: there exists u with pu in F}, and let L_t=|P_t|. If full-search semantics require distinct states for all live prefixes at cut t and, when a dead prefix exists, at least one additional state code unused by live prefixes, then any S-bit state encoding satisfies 2^S >= L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. Consequently S >= max_t ceil(log2(L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t})). In particular, if a specified family has L_t=38 at a cut with t=7, then S>=ceil(log2 38)=6. Proof: the semantics demand L_t pairwise distinct codes for live prefixes. If L_t<2^t, at least one dead prefix exists and its required code is outside those L_t codes, so at least L_t+1 distinct codes are used. An S-bit register has only 2^S codes, proving the inequality at each cut. Maximizing gives the bound; the consequence follows from 32<38<=64. Scope: this is a state-capacity lower bound only; it gives no update-gate lower bound or fixed-(S,D) Pareto optimum.

label: S0378
statement: statement: Zero-gate complete-level obstruction. Fix N input bits and a deterministic time-varying streaming transducer with S state bits and fixed initial state. If every update uses only wires and constants (zero nonconstant gates), then after reading t bits each state coordinate is a constant or one of the t input bits. If the live-prefix set at cut t is all of {0,1}^t and distinct live prefixes must have distinct states, then S >= t. Proof: At each update, an output coordinate is either a constant or copies one coordinate of the prior state or the new input bit. Induction shows that after t updates each coordinate is constant or copies one of the first t input bits. If S<t, at least one of those t positions is not copied by any state coordinate. Two prefixes differing only at that position then produce the same state, contradicting injectivity on the complete live-prefix level. This concerns only zero-gate updates, a fixed initial state, and a complete live-prefix level; it gives no bound for positive gate cost or decoder complexity.

statement: statement: Canonical residual transition circuit upper bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let D_t be the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu in F} at cut t, with r_t=ceil(log_2 D_t). Encode each residual injectively by r_t bits. For each t<N there is a fan-in-two Boolean circuit mapping each reachable encoded residual and next input bit to the encoded next residual, with at most r_{t+1}(2D_t r_t+2D_t-1) AND/OR gates, plus shared input/complement wires; in particular it is a valid exact streaming representation on live prefixes. Proof: each reachable residual R and bit b determines the unique next residual R_b={v:bv in R}; thus each next-code coordinate is a Boolean function on at most 2D_t reachable pairs (code(R),b). Extend that coordinate by zero on all other input strings. Its DNF is the OR of at most 2D_t conjunctions, one conjunction per pair on which it is 1. Each conjunction uses at most r_t+1 literals, hence at most r_t two-input AND gates; an OR of at most 2D_t terms uses at most 2D_t-1 two-input OR gates. Summing over r_{t+1} output bits yields the bound. The construction is correct on every live prefix by the definition of R_b. No claim is made for dead-prefix separation or the full SEARCH semantics.

statement: statement: Residual one-hot update circuit bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At cut t<N, let R_t be its D_t distinct suffix residuals, and encode each residual by its one-hot vector in {0,1}^{D_t}; the input prefix state is promised to be one of these vectors. There is a transition circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with fan-out free, that maps each valid one-hot residual and next input bit b to the one-hot vector of the resulting residual at cut t+1, using at most 3D_t+5D_{t+1} gates, hence at most 13D_t gates. Proof: For each b and next residual j, let A_{b,j} be the set of old residual indices whose b-successor is j. Form h_{b,j}=OR_{i in A_{b,j}} x_i, taking the empty OR as 0. Compute all complements NOT x_i once (D_t gates). For each pair (b,j) with a nonempty A_{b,j}, compute the OR with De Morgan using at most |A_{b,j}|-1 AND gates on the complemented inputs and one NOT gate for the output; singleton ORs require no gates. Summed over b,j, the AND count is at most 2D_t and the output-NOT count at most 2D_{t+1}. Then for each j compute y_j=h_{0,j} XOR (b AND (h_{0,j} XOR h_{1,j})), at most three gates; this is the Boolean mux selecting the b-successor. Total is at most D_t+2D_t+2D_{t+1}+3D_{t+1}=3D_t+5D_{t+1}. Since every next residual has at least one predecessor pair (i,b), D_{t+1}<=2D_t, giving 13D_t. On valid one-hot inputs exactly one source residual is active and exactly one output successor coordinate is active, so this transition is correct. Scope: membership-language streaming with canonical one-hot residual states; no full-search output decoder, dead-prefix state requirement, fixed-width Pareto optimality, or P vs NP consequence is claimed.

statement: statement: Residual-count bound with explicit empty residual. For every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t in {0,...,N}, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} and D_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Then D_t <= min(2^t, |F|+1). Proof: there are 2^t prefixes, so D_t<=2^t. Every nonempty residual occurs at a live prefix. At a fixed cut, each live prefix is a prefix of at least one member of F, and distinct prefixes of the same length cannot be prefixes of the same full string; choosing one member per live prefix therefore injects the set of live prefixes into F. Thus there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. There is at most one empty residual, so D_t<=|F|+1. Combining the inequalities proves the claim. Scope: this bounds canonical residual-representation width only; it gives no update-circuit gate bound.

statement: statement: Transition-table synthesis bound. Let S>=1, let Q be any set of m distinct S-bit states, and let T:Q×{0,1}→{0,1}^S be any prescribed transition map. Over the basis AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, there is a circuit agreeing with T on Q×{0,1} using at most (S+1)+S(4m−1) nonconstant gates. Proof: For each q∈Q and b∈{0,1}, form the indicator I_{q,b}(z,x) of the input pair (q,b), by ANDing the S literals specifying z=q with the literal specifying x=b. The S+1 input negations are shared across all indicators. Each indicator uses S AND gates, so all 2m indicators use at most 2mS gates. For output coordinate j, XOR the indicators I_{q,b} for exactly those pairs where T(q,b)_j=1. The indicators are mutually exclusive on every input, so this XOR equals the desired output on Q×{0,1}; it uses at most 2m−1 XOR gates. Across S coordinates this costs at most S(2m−1) gates. Including the S+1 shared negations gives (S+1)+2mS+S(2m−1)=(S+1)+S(4m−1). The circuit may have arbitrary values outside Q×{0,1}, which are irrelevant to the stated agreement guarantee. Scope: an upper bound for a prescribed finite transition table; it is not an optimality result and gives no lower bound on G_max.

statement: Reachable-transition-table synthesis bound in the AND/XOR/NOT basis. statement: statement: Layer-width lower bound for full-search streaming. Let F be a family of M distinct N-bit truth tables, and let L_t be the number of distinct length-t prefixes occurring among members of F. Suppose a deterministic full-search transducer reads N bits and, at each cut t, assigns distinct S-bit states to all live prefixes and assigns at least one state to every dead prefix, with live and dead states disjoint. Then 2^S >= L_t + 1 whenever L_t < 2^t, and 2^S >= L_t whenever L_t=2^t. Consequently S >= ceil(log2(L_t + [L_t < 2^t])) for every t. Proof: there are 2^S possible states. The L_t live prefixes require L_t distinct states. If L_t<2^t, a dead prefix exists and its state must be distinct from all live states, requiring L_t+1 states. If L_t=2^t, the live prefixes alone require L_t states. Taking base-2 logarithms and using integral S gives the claim. This is only a state-width lower bound; it places no restriction on G_max or D.

label: S0399
statement: Lemma (residual-state lower bound). Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix 0<=t<=N. For each length-t prefix p define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let D_t be the number of distinct such residuals. Every deterministic streaming machine that exactly decides membership in F has at least D_t distinct states after t input bits, hence at least ceil(log_2 D_t) state bits. Proof: If R_t(p) != R_t(q), their symmetric difference contains a suffix u. Exactly one of pu,qu is in F. If the machine reaches the same state after p and q, determinism implies that after reading the common suffix u it reaches the same final state and gives the same answer on both strings, contradicting exact recognition. Thus each distinct residual must correspond to a distinct state. This is an exact lower bound on state count; it does not imply an update-gate lower bound.

label: S0409
statement: statement: For a transition level with L live prefixes encoded by distinct 4-bit states and one reserved dead state, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR transition circuit using at most 4(10(L+1)-1) gates that sends every live prefix/input pair to its correct next state and the dead state to the dead state. In particular, the bound is 556 gates for L=13 and 596 for L=14. Proof: There are at most 2(L+1) specified state/input pairs. For each of the four output coordinates, extend its specified values by zero on all other inputs. A DNF for that coordinate has at most 2(L+1) terms. Each term is a conjunction of at most five literals (four state bits and the input bit), so it takes at most four two-input AND gates. Combining at most 2(L+1) terms takes at most 2(L+1)-1 OR gates. Summing over four coordinates gives 4(8(L+1)+2(L+1)-1)=4(10(L+1)-1). The construction agrees with every specified transition, including both transitions from the dead state. This is an upper bound, not an exact minimum.

statement: statement: For a transition level with L live prefixes encoded by distinct 4-bit states and one reserved dead state, let T=2(L+1), the number of specified pairs (state,input bit). In the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, with fan-out free, the specified transition map has a circuit of at most 28T-7 gates. Proof: For each of the four output coordinates, extend its specified values by zero to all 5-bit inputs. For every specified pair on which that coordinate is 1, form its 5-literal minterm, using shared complements of the five input literals and at most four AND gates per minterm. There are at most T such minterms. Combine them by a binary OR tree; each OR is implemented as (a XOR b) XOR (a AND b), costing three gates, so at most 3(T-1) gates per output. An empty OR is constant 0. Share the five input complements across all outputs. Total cost is at most 4(4T+3(T-1))+5=28T-7. This realizes every specified live and dead transition. Thus the bound is 777 for L=13 and 833 for L=14. This is only an upper bound; it neither determines the minimum nor closes the exact-synthesis gap.

statement: Residual-state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. statement: Zero-update criterion for a fixed encoding. Let F be a finite language of binary strings of length N, and for each t let c_t be an injective encoding of its live length-t prefixes into {0,1}^S, with one additional code d_t reserved for all dead prefixes. Suppose for every t<N and every reachable live state q=c_t(p), the two required successor codes c_{t+1}(pb) when pb is live, and d_{t+1} otherwise, are each either a constant vector or a coordinate projection of (q_1,...,q_S,b); suppose also that the required successor of d_t on each b is d_{t+1} and is of the same form. Then the transducer implements exact full-SEARCH live/dead separation with zero nonconstant gates per update. Proof: For each output coordinate j, select its stipulated constant or input wire among q_1,...,q_S,b. That wire realizes the required jth output on every reachable state/input pair, including the dead state. Combining the S selected wires gives the stipulated successor vector, hence each live prefix follows its prescribed injective code and every dead prefix enters the reserved dead code. Induction on t proves the invariant at all cuts. The decoder is independent and must still be measured as D; the result is only a zero-update sufficient condition at the stated fixed S and does not establish that an SC_{n,s} instance satisfies it or that its Pareto point is optimal.

statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and t in {0,...,N}. For each prefix p of length t, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and let D_t be the number of distinct such residuals. Then D_t <= min(2^t, |F|+1). Proof: There are 2^t prefixes, hence at most 2^t residuals. Call a prefix live if it extends to a member of F. Each live prefix p has a nonempty residual; choose one member f_p of F extending p. If p and q are distinct prefixes of length t, their length-t initial segments differ, so f_p != f_q. Thus the chosen members inject the live prefixes into F, and there are at most |F| live prefixes and at most |F| nonempty residuals. All dead prefixes have empty residual, so they contribute at most one further residual. Hence D_t <= |F|+1 as well. This also covers F empty: there is exactly one residual, the empty set. The finite verification cm-4d9bf9af55334fb3 exhaustively checked all 256 subsets of {0,1}^3 at all four cuts and found no counterexample; the proof itself is general.

statement: Dead-separated one-hot transition bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and at each cut t let P_t be the live prefixes of F and L_t=|P_t|. Use one-hot states for the L_t live prefixes and one additional dead label, represented by L_t+1 bits. At step t<N, the transition on a state label and input bit is realizable by a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit with fan-out free and shared complemented wires, using at most 3(L_t+1)+5(L_{t+1}+1) gates. It sends p to pb if pb is live, otherwise to dead; dead maps to dead. Proof: For each b and next label q, let A_{b,q} be old labels mapping to q; define h_{b,q}=OR_{r in A_{b,q}} x_r (empty OR=0). For a valid one-hot input these indicators exactly identify the successor under b. For each b the nonempty A_{b,q} partition the L_t+1 old labels. Compute all these ORs using shared NOTs of the old bits (L_t+1 gates total), De Morgan ANDs (at most 2(L_t+1) total across b,q, since each partition's sum of |A|-1 is at most L_t), and output NOTs (at most 2(L_{t+1}+1)). Then choose b's successor indicators per q by the mux h_{0,q} OR (b AND h_{1,q}), costing at most 3 gates per q in the allowed AND/OR/NOT basis. Total is at most 3(L_t+1)+5(L_{t+1}+1). Exactly one successor indicator is selected, proving correctness and dead/live separation by induction.

statement: statement: Sharper dead-separated one-hot transition bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N; at cut t let P_t be its live prefixes, L_t=|P_t|, and add one dead label. For each nonempty block of size k, its OR costs at most k-1 AND gates on complemented literals and one NOT gate; singleton blocks need no gate. For each b, the total AND cost is sum_blocks(k-1)=(L_t+1)-number_of_blocks <= L_t, so across b it is at most 2L_t. The output NOT cost is at most the number of nonempty blocks, at most 2(L_{t+1}+1). Finally y_q=h_{0,q} OR (b AND h_{1,q}) uses at most two gates per q, hence at most 2(L_{t+1}+1). Empty blocks use constant 0 and need no gate. For a valid one-hot input exactly one old coordinate is 1, so h_{b,q} is 1 exactly for its prescribed successor q; the mux therefore outputs precisely that successor's one-hot vector. statement: statement: Decoder lookup upper bound for a finite full-SEARCH machine. Let F be a finite set of L valid terminal strings, each assigned a distinct S-bit state, and assign one additional distinct S-bit state to rejection; assume 2^S >= L+1. If each valid state has a prescribed W-bit output and rejection outputs 0^W, then with fan-out free the decoder has an AND/XOR/NOT circuit of at most S+(L+1)(S-1)+2W(L+1) gates. Proof: Compute the S complemented state-input literals once, using S NOT gates. For each of the K=L+1 specified states, compute its equality indicator by ANDing its S matching literals, using S-1 gates per state. The indicators are mutually exclusive. For each output coordinate, OR the indicators of valid states whose prescribed bit is 1, using at most 2K gates by De Morgan; an empty OR is constant 0. Thus the output is correct on every specified state and the total is S+K(S-1)+2WK. This is an explicit decoder-cost upper bound for a fixed assignment, not an optimality or asymptotic claim.

statement: statement: Exclusive-indicator decoder bound. Let K>=1 specified S-bit terminal states be distinct, with one designated rejection state, and let each of the other states carry a prescribed W-bit output. For S>=1, a decoder over AND, XOR, NOT, constants, and free fan-out computes the prescribed outputs on all K states using at most S+K(S-1)+W(K-1) gates. Proof: Compute the S complemented input literals using S NOT gates. For each specified state, compute its equality indicator as the AND of its S matching literals, using S-1 two-input AND gates. These K indicators are mutually exclusive on the specified states, with exactly one equal to 1. For each output coordinate, XOR the indicators of the specified states whose prescribed bit is 1; because the indicators are mutually exclusive, the XOR equals their OR and yields the required bit. If q indicators are selected, this uses max(q-1,0)<=K-1 XOR gates. Rejection's output is prescribed as zero, so it is omitted from each selected set. Summing gives S+K(S-1)+W(K-1). label: S0425
statement: statement: Zero-gate restriction characterization. Let U be any set of specified input points in {0,1}^k, and let f:U->{0,1}^w be a partially specified transition map. In the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, with every nonconstant gate counted and fan-out free, f has a zero-gate implementation on U if and only if each output coordinate f_j agrees on U with either a constant function or one of the k input-coordinate projections. Proof: A circuit with zero nonconstant gates can only connect each output to a constant or an available input wire, proving necessity. Conversely, for each output coordinate choose the matching constant or input wire and connect it directly to that output; free fan-out permits reuse, proving sufficiency. The characterization applies to any specified reachable state/input pairs, including redundant encodings and don't-care inputs outside U. It is only a zero-gate test and gives no positive-gate lower bound or decoder-cost conclusion.

label: S0426
statement:
statement: Dead-prefix state-count lower bound and sharpness. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: there exists u with pu in F}. In any deterministic streaming machine whose state after prefix p must distinguish each p in P_t from every dead prefix at the same cut, the number of states at cut t is at least |P_t|+1, hence S >= ceil(log2(max_t(|P_t|+1))) state bits. Conversely, if the machine is allowed time-dependent transition functions and has S=ceil(log2(max_t(|P_t|+1))) bits, there exists a correct live/dead separating machine: injectively assign distinct codes at each cut to P_t and one dead class, and define each transition on live codes by the actual prefix extension (live successor code if the extension remains in P_{t+1}, otherwise the next dead code), and on the dead code by the next dead code; define it arbitrarily elsewhere. This establishes that the state-bit threshold in the Lemma M model is necessary and sufficient for the abstract transition-table model, while saying nothing about Boolean gate cost.
evidence: Lower bound: at cut t, the |P_t| live prefixes have pairwise distinguishable required states, and a dead prefix must have a state distinct from all of them. Thus at least |P_t|+1 states are required. For sufficiency, the capacity condition lets us assign distinct codes at every cut to all live prefixes and one dead class. Each live code/input-bit transition is assigned the code for its extension if live, and the reserved next-cut dead code otherwise; the dead code transitions to the next dead code. Induction on prefix length verifies the machine's state on every prefix. This constructs transition tables but does not establish any circuit gate bound.

label: S0427
statement:
statement: Corrected per-cut state-capacity theorem. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, P_t={p in {0,1}^t: some u has pu in F}, and D_t={0,1}^t\P_t. In the explicit prefix-identity model, where distinct live prefixes at cut t must have distinct states and every dead prefix must have a state distinct from every live prefix, the minimum number of states at cut t is |P_t|+1 if D_t is nonempty, and |P_t| if D_t is empty. Consequently the exact minimum uniform state-bit count for time-dependent transition tables is ceil(log2(max_t (|P_t|+1_{D_t nonempty}))).
evidence: Lower bound: the |P_t| live prefixes require pairwise distinct states by the model, and if D_t is nonempty, any dead prefix requires one further state distinct from all live states; if D_t is empty there is no dead-prefix constraint and the |P_t| live states suffice. For the matching upper bound, at each cut assign distinct codes to the live prefixes and, exactly when D_t is nonempty, one shared code to all dead prefixes. For each input bit, define the next state of a live prefix code as the code of its extension if live and otherwise the next cut's dead code; define a dead code's next state to be the next dead code. When a cut has no dead prefixes, only live transitions occur from reachable states. Extend the transition arbitrarily to unreachable state/input pairs. Induction over t gives the prescribed live/dead state on every prefix. This proves the table-model characterization, without asserting any Boolean gate bound.

label: S0428
statement: statement: Fixed-encoding transition-table synthesis bound. Let a deterministic streaming transition from S-bit states and one input bit have r reachable state/input pairs, and fix any prescribed next-state encoding on those pairs. For each next-state output coordinate j, let k_j be the number of prescribed pairs whose output bit is 1. There is a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit computing all prescribed outputs on the reachable pairs, with at most sum_j (min(k_j,r-k_j)(S+1)) gates, using shared input literals and constants; its behavior outside those pairs is unrestricted. Proof: for coordinate j, if k_j <= r-k_j, form one equality indicator for each of its k_j positive rows by ANDing the S state literals and the input literal (at most S two-input AND gates per row), then OR the indicators with at most k_j-1 two-input OR gates; this uses at most k_j(S+1) gates. If r-k_j < k_j, perform the same construction for zero rows and negate the resulting OR, using at most (r-k_j)(S+1)+1 gates; the displayed looser bound can absorb this final NOT when S>=1, since S+1>=2. Summing the coordinate circuits proves the claim. This is an upper bound for fixed encodings only; it neither optimizes the encoding nor supplies a lower bound on G_max.

label: S0457
statement: Lemma (G=1 transition structure, corrected). Let F: {0,1}^S × {0,1} → {0,1}^S be computed by a circuit over basis {AND, OR, XOR, NOT, constants} with exactly one non-free gate, where NOT is free (applied to inputs without cost) and the non-free gate has fan-in 2. Then there exists a two-literal gate g = op(l₁, l₂) with op ∈ {AND, OR, XOR} and l₁, l₂ literals of (q, b) or constants, such that every output coordinate F_j is either a base literal (q_i, ¬q_i, b, ¬b), a constant (0, 1), or ±g. Equivalently, F lies in the set G1_S = { wiring of base literals/constants to outputs } ∪ { same with any subset of coordinates replaced by +g or −g for one shared gate g = op(l₁, l₂) }. Proof: Each output wire of the circuit is either (a) connected directly to an input/constant (possibly with free NOT), yielding a base literal or constant, or (b) connected to the output of the unique non-free gate g. Since g has fan-in 2 and its inputs are free (literals/constants), g = op(l₁, l₂) for literals l₁, l₂. By fan-out, the output of g can drive any number of output coordinates, each optionally negated by a free NOT. No other non-literal function exists in the circuit. Hence every coordinate is base or ±g. The set I = {j : F_j = ±g} is exactly the set of coordinates driven by g; its size is unconstrained (0 ≤ |I| ≤ S). ∎ This corrects S0014 (which falsely claimed |I|≤1) and S0069 (which had a count error: 60 not 120 for S=2). Verified by exhaustive enumeration cm-3c1e9d5b0e2f4e9c for S=2,3.

label: S0458
statement:
statement: Residual-state lower bound for deterministic streaming membership. Let N be a positive integer, F ⊆ {0,1}^N, and let a deterministic streaming machine read the input from left to right, with state after t bits determined by the length-t prefix and a fixed decoder that decides membership in F from the final state. For each t ∈ {0,…,N} and prefix p ∈ {0,1}^t, define R_t(p) = {u ∈ {0,1}^{N−t} : pu ∈ F}. Then the machine has at least |{R_t(p) : p ∈ {0,1}^t}| distinct reachable states after t bits.
proof: Suppose prefixes p and p′ reach the same state after t bits. For every suffix u of length N−t, determinism implies that processing u from either state reaches the same final state, so the decoder gives the same membership answer for pu and p′u. Therefore pu ∈ F iff p′u ∈ F for every such u, and hence R_t(p)=R_t(p′). Taking the contrapositive, prefixes with distinct residual sets must reach distinct states. One state per distinct residual set is therefore necessary.
scope: This proves a state-count lower bound for deterministic streaming membership machines only. It gives no transition-circuit gate-cost lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

label: S0460
statement:
statement: Search-state injectivity for live prefixes. Let F be a set of binary strings of common length N. A deterministic one-pass machine reads a string left to right and, from its final state, either rejects strings outside F or outputs a witness that computes the entire input string for every input in F. At any fixed t, distinct live prefixes p and p' (each having at least one completion in F) must reach distinct states.
proof: Suppose distinct live prefixes p,p' at length t reach the same state. If their residual completion sets differ, choose a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pu,p'u belongs to F. Since the same state followed by the same suffix gives the same final state, the decoder must give the same answer on both, contradicting correct membership/rejection. If their residual completion sets are equal, that set is nonempty because both prefixes are live. Choose any u in the common residual set. Both pu and p'u belong to F, but they are distinct strings because p != p'. The shared intermediate state and common suffix again give the same final state, so the decoder outputs the same witness on both. A witness computing the entire input cannot compute two distinct truth tables, contradiction. Therefore the states differ.
scope: Exact deterministic witness-search semantics with a decoder that correctly rejects nonmembers and outputs a witness computing the full input for every member. This is a state-injectivity lemma for live prefixes; it implies at least L_t reachable states when L_t live prefixes exist. It gives no transition-circuit gate-cost lower bound and says nothing about decoder size.

statement:
statement: Residual-class transition upper bound. For every finite language F subset {0,1}^N, put R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} and K=max_{0<=t<=N}|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. There is an exact deterministic layered membership machine with S=ceil(log2 K) state bits and at most O(S*2^S) AND/OR gates per update, allowing NOT gates at zero cost; the final decoder is a Boolean function on S bits.
proof: At layer t encode each distinct reachable residual R_t(p) by a distinct S-bit code. For b in {0,1}, define delta_t(R,b)={u:bu in R}. If R=R_t(p), then delta_t(R,b)=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined on reachable codes. Define it arbitrarily on unused codes. Each of its S output bits is a Boolean function on S+1 inputs. Its disjunctive normal form has at most 2^(S+1) input minterms, each requiring O(S) AND gates and O(2^S) OR gates, hence O(S*2^S) gates per output and O(S*2^S) only if the output count is absorbed incorrectly; explicitly the safe bound is O(S^2*2^S) total gates per update. The decoder labels each terminal residual by whether it contains the empty suffix; this equals membership in F. Therefore the machine is exact.
scope: Finite-language membership transducers; layered transitions may depend on t; free NOT; decoder cost unrestricted. The bound is a general constructive upper bound, not a lower bound and not a fixed-(S,D) Pareto result.

statement:
statement: Shared-minterm residual-transition upper bound. For every finite language F subset {0,1}^N, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, K=max_t |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|, and S=ceil(log2 K). proof: At level t assign distinct S-bit codes to the K_t reachable residuals. For b in {0,1}, define delta_t(R,b)={u:bu in R}. If R=R_t(p), then delta_t(R,b)=R_{t+1}(pb), so this transition is well-defined on reachable codes; extend it arbitrarily elsewhere. Each transition is a Boolean map on k=S+1 inputs with S output bits. For every a in {0,1}^k construct the indicator minterm m_a for input a, using O(k) AND gates per minterm and O(k*2^k) gates total. Share these minterms across all outputs. Each output is the OR of at most 2^k selected minterms, requiring O(2^k) OR gates, hence O(S*2^k) for all S outputs. As k=S+1, the total is O(S*2^S). At the terminal level, decode a residual as accepting exactly when it contains the empty suffix; this is membership in F.

This does not bound dead/live separation gate complexity in Lemma M's witness-search model or establish P-vs-NP progress.

There is an exact deterministic layered membership machine using S state bits and O(S*2^S) AND/OR gates per update; shared gates are counted once and the final decoder is unrestricted.
proof: At level t assign distinct S-bit codes to the K_t reachable residuals. For b in {0,1}, define delta_t(R,b)={u:bu in R}. If R=R_t(p), then delta_t(R,b)=R_{t+1}(pb), so this transition is well-defined on reachable codes; extend it arbitrarily elsewhere. Each transition is a Boolean map on k=S+1 inputs with S output bits. For every a in {0,1}^k construct the indicator minterm m_a for input a, using O(k) AND gates per minterm and O(k*2^k) gates total. Share these minterms across all outputs. Each output is the OR of at most 2^k selected minterms, requiring O(2^k) OR gates, hence O(S*2^k) for all S outputs. As k=S+1, the total is O(S*2^S). At the terminal level, decode a residual as accepting exactly when it contains the empty suffix; this is membership in F.
scope: Finite-language deterministic layered streaming membership; time-dependent transitions; arbitrary encodings of reachable residuals; shared AND/OR gates counted once; unrestricted final decoder. This does not bound dead/live separation gate complexity in Lemma M's witness-search model or establish P-vs-NP progress.

label: S0463
statement: statement: Universal transition-table upper bound. For S>=1, every map T:{0,1}^S x {0,1}->{0,1}^S has a circuit of at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates, with NOT and constants free. Proof: Put d=S+1. For one output coordinate with k accepting inputs, form a d-literal minterm for each accepting input, using at most d-1 AND gates per minterm, and OR the k terms using k-1 OR gates. The cost is k(d-1)+(k-1)=kd-1 when k>0, and zero when k=0; in either case it is at most d*2^d. Implement the S outputs separately, giving at most S*d*2^d gates. The circuit takes the state and arriving bit together as inputs, so symbol selection is included. Scope: arbitrary finite transition tables in this basis; this is an upper bound, not an optimal Pareto point or lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

label: S0464
statement:
statement: Wire-only coordinate representation lemma. Let a deterministic layered streaming transducer read x_1,...,x_N, have S Boolean state bits, and use updates in which every new state bit is either a constant, a copy of one old state bit, or a copy of the newly read input bit. For each time t, every state bit is a constant or a projection x_i with i<=t. Consequently, there is a set I_t subseteq {1,...,t} of at most S input coordinates such that the state after t is determined by x|_{I_t}; if the machine's states are injective on a family A_t of live length-t prefixes, then coordinate projection x -> x|_{I_t} is injective on A_t.
proof: Induct on t. At t=0 each state bit is initialized to a fixed constant, hence has the claimed form. Suppose the claim holds after t bits. At the next update, each bit either remains a constant, copies an old bit (which by induction is a constant or one of x_1,...,x_t), or copies x_{t+1}; thus every bit after t+1 is a constant or one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. Let I_t consist of the indices of the nonconstant projections appearing among the S state bits; then |I_t|<=S and the entire state is determined by x|_{I_t}. If two members of A_t have the same restriction to I_t, their state vectors are equal. Injectivity of states on A_t therefore implies the two prefixes are equal, proving that the restriction map is injective on A_t.
scope: Zero-gate wire/constant updates only, with possibly time-dependent choices of wires; applies to any live-prefix family for which state injectivity is required. No positive-gate lower bound, decoder-size bound, or P-vs-NP implication.

label: S0465
statement: statement: For any deterministic streaming transducer with m states and a binary input alphabet, the one-hot encoding q_i=[state=i] updates each next-state bit by next_j = OR_{i,b:delta(i,b)=j}(q_i AND [input=b]); this computes the exact transition and has fan-in-2 AND/XOR/NOT circuit size O(m^2) per symbol.

structure.evidence: For a valid one-hot state, exactly one q_i is 1, and for a binary input exactly one symbol indicator is 1. Therefore next_j is 1 exactly when the unique state-symbol pair maps to j, so the output is the one-hot successor state. Each of m output bits is an OR of at most 2m pairwise conjunctions; with fan-in-2 AND/NOT, De Morgan implements each OR using O(m) gates, giving O(m^2) total. This is a general proof; the requested finite experiment is still pending.

label: S0466
statement: statement: For every deterministic transducer with state set [m] and binary input alphabet {0,1}, there is an exact one-hot encoded transition circuit with at most 5m-1 binary gates from AND, OR, NOT, counting NOT as a gate, if constants are free; behavior on non-one-hot encodings is unrestricted.

structure.evidence: Proof: Let q_i be the one-hot indicators of the current state and x the input. For b in {0,1} and j in [m], set A_{b,j}=OR_{i:delta(i,b)=j} q_i, with an empty OR equal to the free constant 0. The nonempty fibers of delta_b partition [m]. If there are r_b nonempty fibers, all their ORs can be computed using sum_j (|fiber_j|-1)=m-r_b<=m-1 binary OR gates. Thus both collections A_{b,j} use at most 2m-2 gates. For each j compute q'_j=(NOT x AND A_{0,j}) OR (x AND A_{1,j}), using two AND gates and one OR gate, for 3m gates total. One NOT gate computes NOT x and is shared. Total: (2m-2)+3m+1=5m-1. On a valid one-hot q, exactly one q_i is 1, so A_{b,j}=1 exactly when delta_b maps the current state to j; the displayed mux outputs exactly the one-hot successor. This proves the claimed gate bound and exactness.

label: S0468
statement: statement: Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N and fix t. In every deterministic one-pass streaming membership machine for F, if there is at least one live length-t prefix and at least one dead length-t prefix, then at least two distinct states are reachable after t bits. Proof: choose a live prefix p and dead prefix q. By liveness there is a suffix u of length N-t with pu in F. Since q is dead, qu is not in F. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would make processing the common suffix u end in the same state, so the fixed membership decoder would give the same answer on pu and qu, contradicting that exactly one belongs to F. Hence the two prefixes reach different states. More strongly, this argument separates every live prefix state from every dead prefix state. Scope: membership only; it yields a 2-state lower bound at a mixed layer, not the live-prefix-count bound or any transition-gate lower bound.

label: S0469
statement: statement: For every N>=2 and every word w in {0,1}^N, the exact one-pass membership language F={w} has minimum worst-layer update cost G_max=1 among deterministic layered machines with one state bit, initial state 1, fixed final decoder, basis AND/XOR/NOT/constants, free wires and fanout, and every nonconstant AND/XOR gate counted. Proof: The canonical machine stores q=1 iff the prefix read so far equals the corresponding prefix of w. At layer i, set q'=q AND (b if w_i=1, else NOT b), and accept iff q=1 at the end. This is exact on every input and uses one AND gate per layer i>=2; the first layer can use a wire or its negation from the fixed initial state, so G_max<=1. For the lower bound, at any layer i>=2 correctness forces the output on reachable states q and input b to be q AND (b if w_i=1, else NOT b): q=0 must remain dead for both b values, while q=1 remains live exactly on the matching b. This function is not a wire, constant, or literal, so zero nonconstant AND/XOR gates cannot compute it. Thus that layer costs at least one gate and G_max>=1.

label: S0470
statement: statement: For every N>=2 and word w in {0,1}^N, the singleton language F={w} has a deterministic layered one-bit streaming membership machine with G_max<=2 when the basis is AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, every nonconstant gate including NOT is counted, wires and fanout are free, the initial state is fixed to 1, and the final decoder accepts state 1. Proof: After reading i bits, let q_i=1 exactly when the read prefix equals w_1...w_i. At layer i (1-indexed), update q_i=q_{i-1} AND b_i if w_i=1; this uses one AND gate. If w_i=0, update q_i=q_{i-1} AND NOT(b_i); this uses one NOT and one AND gate. The induction invariant q_i=1 iff the prefix matches holds from q_0=1, so the final decoder decides membership exactly for every length-N input. Thus each update costs at most two counted gates, and G_max<=2. This is an upper bound only; it makes no optimality claim and does not close the SC_{n,s} Pareto obligation.

label: S0471
statement:
statement: Exact search-state lower bound with dead-prefix separation. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic one-pass transducer reads prefixes and, after N bits, outputs a valid witness computing the entire input if the input lies in F, and rejects otherwise. For each t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes having a completion in F. If at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F, then every such machine has at least L_t+1 distinct states after t bits; if every length-t prefix is live, it has at least L_t.
proof: Fix t. Distinct live prefixes p,p' cannot share a state. If their residual completion sets differ, choose a suffix in their symmetric difference; the same state followed by that suffix would have to both reject and accept. If their residual sets are equal, they are nonempty; choose a common completing suffix u. Then pu and p'u are distinct members of F, yet the same final state would need to output a witness computing both distinct strings. Thus the L_t live prefixes occupy distinct states. Now let d be dead and p live. If they shared a state, choose a suffix u completing p. Processing u from that state ends in one decoder output, which must be a valid witness on pu but rejection on du, since d has no completion. Contradiction. Thus every dead-prefix state is outside the live-state set, yielding one additional state whenever a dead prefix exists.
scope: Exact deterministic one-pass witness-search transducers on fixed-length binary inputs; the final decoder rejects nonmembers and outputs a witness computing the full input on members. This is a state-count lower bound only; it gives no transition-gate or decoder-size bound.

label: S0473
statement: Lemma (shared-minterm transition upper bound). For every integer S≥1 and every map T:{0,1}^{S+1}→{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit computing T with at most (S+1)2^(S+1)+S(2^(S+1)−1) gates, when NOT gates and constants are free. Proof: Put d=S+1 and q=2^d. For each input z∈{0,1}^d, construct its minterm M_z, the conjunction of the d literals specifying z. This takes at most d−1 fan-in-two AND gates per minterm, hence at most (d−1)q gates total. These minterms are shared by all output coordinates. For coordinate i, let A_i={z:T(z)_i=1} and B_i={0,1}^d\A_i. If |A_i|≤|B_i|, output the OR of M_z over z∈A_i; otherwise output the negation of the OR over z∈B_i. The chosen set has size h_i≤q/2, so its OR takes at most max(h_i−1,0)≤q−1 gates; an empty OR is the free constant 0. Summed over S coordinates, this uses at most S(q−1) further gates. Each input has exactly one true minterm, so the selected OR, or its negation, equals the required coordinate on every input. Substituting q=2^(S+1) proves the bound.

For S=3, the separate finite construction-cost comparison is recorded in cm-d022bfeabfa447ec (independently repeated as cm-6fd14530622f4e33); it is finite evidence only and is not needed for the general proof.

label: S0474
statement: statement: For every N>=1 and every language F subset {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic layered streaming search machine with S=N state bits, zero nonconstant update gates, and a final decoder that accepts exactly F and outputs a valid witness for every member, when the witness is the input string itself. At time t its state is the length-N vector consisting of the t-bit prefix followed by N-t zeroes. Initialize to 0^N; at step t+1 copy the first t coordinates by wires, write the arriving bit into coordinate t+1 by a wire, and set later coordinates to zero by free constants. At t=N the state equals the input, so the decoder tests membership in F and, for members, outputs that state. At every t the map from all length-t prefixes to states is injective, so live prefixes have distinct states and any dead-prefix state is disjoint from them. Thus the machine satisfies the SEARCH separation condition with no nonconstant transition gates. The construction requires S=N, so it establishes no bound in the required meaningful regime S<N.

label: S0475
statement: statement: Exact layer width for full deterministic search. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes with a completion in F, and let d_t be 1 iff at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F. In a deterministic layered one-pass machine that rejects inputs outside F and outputs, on each input in F, a witness computing that entire input, the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is exactly L_t+d_t. Consequently the minimum fixed state width is ceil(log2(max_{0<=t<=N}(L_t+d_t))), with width 0 allowed when the maximum is 1. Proof: Any two distinct live prefixes reaching the same state contradict search correctness: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference yields different membership answers from the same final state; if the residual sets agree, their common nonempty residual supplies a suffix for which the same final state would have to output a witness computing two distinct strings. A live and dead prefix cannot share a state: append a suffix completing the live prefix; the resulting identical final state would need both acceptance and rejection. Hence at least L_t+d_t states are necessary. For sufficiency, assign distinct states to live prefixes and one additional state to all dead prefixes when any exist. From each live prefix state, on bit b transition to the state of its extended prefix if live and to the dead state otherwise; the dead state loops to itself. At the final layer, output the witness associated to each member string and reject the dead state. These layer-dependent transitions realize the specification and use exactly L_t+d_t states at layer t. This is a finite-language state-width lemma only; it gives no transition-circuit gate-cost bound.
