label: S0476
statement: statement: Affine syndrome streaming lemma. Let N,m≥0, let H∈GF(2)^{m×N}, and b∈GF(2)^m. For F={x∈{0,1}^N:Hx=b}, there is a deterministic one-pass membership machine using m state bits and at most m nonconstant XOR gates per input-bit update. After reading prefix p of length t, its state is r_t=b−H_{[:,1..t]}p over GF(2). On reading bit z at position t+1, it updates r_{t+1}=r_t−zH_{[:,t+1]}; it accepts at the end iff r_N=0. Thus prefixes with different residual vectors have distinct states, and prefixes with the same residual vector have identical completion sets. The bound holds also when F is empty or H has zero rows. Proof: Initially r_0=b. If r_t=b−H_{[:,1..t]}p, then subtracting z times the next column gives r_{t+1}=b−H_{[:,1..t+1]}(pz), proving the invariant by induction. At t=N, r_N=0 iff Hx=b. Each output coordinate either stays unchanged or XORs its state bit with the arriving bit, so at most one XOR gate per coordinate suffices. For a fixed prefix p, a suffix u completes it iff H_{[:,t+1..N]}u=r_t; hence equal residual vectors give equal completion sets, and unequal residual vectors cannot collide in this encoding. This is an exact membership construction, not a minimum-update-cost result and not a witness decoder.

label: S0477
statement:
statement: Zero-gate streaming-memory characterization. Consider a deterministic binary streaming transducer with a fixed initial state, time-dependent update circuits, and S state bits. Suppose each update is built only from direct wires, constants, and literals (NOT is free), with no AND/OR gates. After reading any prefix, every state bit is either a constant or a literal of one input bit from that prefix. Consequently the machine's state is a tuple of at most S signed input-bit selections and constants; it cannot compute a non-literal function of the prefix during updates.
proof: Induct on the number t of bits read. At t=0, every state bit is fixed by the initial state, hence constant. For the induction step, each output of a zero-AND/OR update is a constant or a literal of one of the S old state bits or the arriving input bit. By the induction hypothesis, a literal of an old state bit is either constant or a literal of an earlier input bit (possibly complemented); a literal of the arriving bit is itself a literal of that bit. Therefore every new state bit has the asserted form. This proves the claim for all t. The tuple has S coordinates, so stores at most S selected signed input bits, though selections may repeat.
scope: Exact deterministic streaming transducers with fixed initial state, arbitrary time-dependent zero-AND/OR transition circuits, direct wires/constants and free NOT; no claim about positive gate cost or about decoder complexity.

label: S0478
statement:
statement: Zero-gate acceptance factorization. Fix a deterministic binary streaming machine with S state bits, fixed initial state, time-dependent updates using only wires, constants, and free NOT, and a terminal decoder. For every input length N there are at most S selected input coordinates (with signs or constants) such that the machine’s acceptance decision depends only on those selected bits. Thus, if two length-N inputs agree on the selected coordinates, the machine accepts either both or neither.
proof: By S0477’s induction, each terminal state coordinate is a constant or a signed copy of one input coordinate. The terminal state is therefore determined by the tuple of at most S such values. The decoder is a function of that tuple, so inputs agreeing on the selected coordinates reach the same terminal state and receive the same decision.
scope: Exact deterministic streaming machines with fixed initial state, time-dependent zero-AND/OR updates, free NOT, and an unrestricted terminal decoder. This is conditional on S0477 and gives no positive gate lower bound unless the selected coordinates can be ruled out for the target language.

label: S0479
statement:
statement: Finite zero-gate obstruction for SC_{3,1}. Let inputs be truth tables of the eight assignments to three Boolean variables, and let SC_{3,1} contain constants, literals, and every truth table computed by one binary Boolean gate on at most two input variables. Any deterministic streaming machine whose state bits are updated using only wires, constants, and free NOT, with S<=6 state bits and an arbitrary terminal decoder, fails to decide membership in SC_{3,1}.
proof: By induction on the number of stream bits read, each state bit is a constant or a signed copy of one input coordinate: this holds initially, and a wire or negation of such a bit or the arriving bit preserves the property. Thus after all eight bits the terminal state depends on at most S<=6 input coordinates. Choose a coordinate i not retained. The zero truth table and the unit-vector truth table e_i agree on every retained coordinate. The zero table is in SC_{3,1}. The table e_i is not: as a function on the three input variables it is 1 at exactly one assignment, so changing each of the three variables from that assignment changes its value; hence it depends essentially on all three variables, whereas a constant, literal, or one binary gate on at most two variables depends on at most two. The decoder must give the same answer on the two streams, contradicting correct membership decisions.
scope: Finite decision problem SC_{3,1} on eight-bit truth tables; fixed initial state, time-dependent zero-AND/OR updates, free NOT, unrestricted terminal decoder. This does not bound positive gate costs or prove a Lemma M asymptotic claim.

label: S0481
statement:
statement: Residual-class transition upper bound. Let N≥0 and F⊆{0,1}^N. For each t and prefix p∈{0,1}^t, let R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}: pu∈F}, and let K=max_t |{R_t(p):p∈{0,1}^t}|. There is an exact deterministic layered membership machine for F with S=ceil(log₂ K) state bits (or one bit when K=1) and at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates per update; NOT and constants are free, and the final decoder is unrestricted.
proof: At layer t, assign an injective S-bit code to each distinct reachable residual R_t(p); this is possible since there are at most K such residuals. For a reachable residual R and input bit b, define its next residual by D_b(R)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t−1}: bu∈R}. If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so this transition depends only on the encoded residual and b, not on the choice of p. Define transitions arbitrarily on unused state codes. For each of the S output bits of a transition map on S+1 input bits, let A be its accepting input assignments. If A is empty, output the constant 0. Otherwise, form one minterm per assignment in A using at most S AND gates per minterm, then OR the |A| minterms using at most |A|−1 OR gates. Since |A|≤2^(S+1), each output uses at most (S+1)2^(S+1) gates; all S outputs use at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). At layer N, the residual is either {ε} or empty, and membership in F is exactly whether it is {ε}; the decoder can therefore return the correct answer. If K=1, use S=1 to avoid a zero-bit encoding; the same construction applies.
scope: Finite binary languages; deterministic layered membership; layer-dependent transitions; unrestricted decoder; NOT/constants free. This is an upper bound only and does not determine minimal G_max or establish a lower bound.

label: S0483
statement: statement: Dead-prefix strengthening of live-state injectivity. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and consider a deterministic one-pass machine that, after reading the full input, rejects every string outside F and outputs a witness computing the entire input string for every string in F. At layer t, let L_t be the number of prefixes p of length t having at least one completion in F. If at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F, then the machine has at least L_t+1 distinct reachable states after t bits. Proof: First, distinct live prefixes p and p' must reach distinct states. If their residual completion sets differ, choose a suffix in their symmetric difference; identical states followed by that suffix would yield identical final states, contradicting correct membership/rejection. If their residual sets are equal, that set is nonempty; choose a common completing suffix u. Then pu and p'u are distinct members of F, but identical states followed by u yield the same final state and hence the same decoded witness, which cannot compute both distinct truth tables. Thus the L_t live prefixes occupy L_t distinct states. Now fix a dead prefix d and any live prefix p. Choose a suffix u completing p. If d and p shared a state, processing u from the common state would yield the same final state on du and pu; the decoder would have to reject du, which is outside F, and output a valid witness for pu, a contradiction. Therefore the state reached by d is distinct from every live-prefix state, giving at least L_t+1 states. Scope: exact deterministic search semantics with a final decoder; no bound on transition circuit complexity is implied.

label: S0484
statement:
statement: For every integer S>=1 and every map T:{0,1}^S x {0,1}->{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants computing T using at most S(S+1)2^S non-constant gates.
proof: For each output coordinate, its input domain has d=S+1 bits. Choose whichever of the set of accepting assignments and its complement has smaller size k<=2^(d-1). Express the selected set as an OR of k d-literal minterms. Each minterm takes at most d-1 fan-in-two AND gates, and their OR takes at most k-1 OR gates; for k=0 use a constant. The cost is at most dk<=d*2^(d-1). If the selected set was the rejecting set, use a free NOT. Summing over S outputs gives S*d*2^(d-1)=S(S+1)2^S.

label: S0503
statement:
statement: Search-state counting lemma for SC_{3,1}. Let F be any finite family of N-bit strings, and let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes that extend to a member of F. If L_t<2^t, then every deterministic one-pass search transducer that rejects inputs outside F and outputs the full input string as witness on inputs in F needs at least L_t+1 states after t bits. Consequently, if an independent exhaustive enumeration confirms |SC_{3,1}|=38 and L_7=38, such a transducer needs at least 39 states, hence at least 6 state bits, at layer 7.
proof: There are L_t live prefixes. Distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference forces different accept/reject behavior from the same state; if the residual sets agree, the common nonempty residual supplies a suffix completing both prefixes, yielding two distinct valid strings that would produce the same final state and decoded witness. Since L_t<2^t, choose a dead prefix d. For any live prefix p, choose a suffix u completing p. If d and p shared a state, processing u would give the same final state on du and pu, but the decoder must reject du and output the full-string witness on pu. Thus the dead prefix state differs from all L_t live states, so there are at least L_t+1 states. For L_7=38 this is 39 states; 2^5<39<=2^6, requiring at least 6 bits.
scope: Finite deterministic one-pass total search with full input witness decoded from the final state; the numerical SC_{3,1} consequence is conditional on the specified independent enumeration. This gives a state-width lower bound only, not an update-gate lower bound or P!=NP progress.

statement:
statement: Shared-minterm transition synthesis bound. For every integer S>=1 and every map T:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants, sharing gates across outputs, that computes T using at most 3S*2^S-S gates.
proof: Let r=2^S. There are 2r input rows. For every row build its minterm with S fan-in-two AND gates, costing 2rS gates. For each output bit choose the smaller of its 1-set and 0-set, of size h<=r. OR the corresponding shared minterms using at most h-1<=r-1 OR gates, then complement if the 0-set was chosen. Summed over S outputs, the cost is at most 2rS+S(r-1)=3S*2^S-S. This computes every output correctly on every row.
scope: All Boolean transition maps with S state bits and one input bit; fan-in-two AND/OR gates counted globally with sharing, NOT and constants free. Upper bound only.

statement:
statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N, define residuals R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, and K=max_t |{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. There is a deterministic layered membership machine using S=max(1,ceil(log2 K)) state bits and at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) fan-in-two AND/OR gates per update, with free NOT/constants and an unrestricted final decoder.

If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so its next code is determined by the current code and b. Define outputs arbitrarily on unused codes. Each output bit is a Boolean function on S+1 inputs. Implement it as an OR of minterms for its satisfying inputs; each minterm uses at most S binary AND gates, and the OR uses at most 2^(S+1)-1 binary OR gates. Thus the total per output is at most (S+1)2^(S+1), and all S outputs use at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). At t=N, the residual is {epsilon} exactly for members of F and empty otherwise, so the unrestricted decoder decides membership. If K=1, S=1 gives a valid encoding and the same argument applies.

statement:
statement: Two-word streaming membership lemma. Let N>=1 and let x,y be distinct words in {0,1}^N. There is a deterministic layered one-pass membership machine for F={x,y} using two state bits (A,B), initialized to (1,1), with at most two fan-in-two AND gates per update (NOT and constants free), and a final decoder accepting iff A=1 or B=1. At layer i, on input bit b, update A'=A AND [b=x_i] and B'=B AND [b=y_i].
proof: After t bits, A=1 exactly when the prefix read equals x[1..t], and B=1 exactly when it equals y[1..t]. This holds at t=0 because both empty prefixes match. If it holds at t, matching the next prefix is equivalent to matching the existing prefix and matching the next bit to x_{t+1} or y_{t+1}; the displayed updates implement those conjunctions. At t=N, A or B is 1 exactly for inputs x or y, so the decoder recognizes F. Each predicate [b=c] is b or NOT b, requiring no counted gate; each output uses one AND gate. Thus each update uses at most two counted gates.
scope: Exact deterministic layered membership for any two-element language over {0,1}^N; time-dependent transitions; two state bits; fan-in-two AND/XOR basis with free NOT and constants; unrestricted final decoder. Upper bound only; no lower bound or result for SC_{n,s}.

statement:
statement: Finite search-state lower bound for SC_{3,1} at the 7-bit prefix layer. Let F be the set of the 38 truth tables in SC_{3,1} on three inputs, and consider any deterministic one-pass search machine that accepts exactly F and whose final decoder outputs a valid truth-table witness for every member of F. At layer t=7, the machine has at least 39 reachable states, hence at least 6 state bits.
proof: There are 2^7=128 binary prefixes of length 7. The exact SC_{3,1} enumeration gives 38 distinct live prefixes at this layer, so at least one prefix is dead. Distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states: if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference makes identical states give different required decisions. If their residual sets agree, choose a common completing suffix; the two resulting inputs are distinct members of F, so a shared state would force the decoder to output one witness for two different truth tables. A dead prefix must also have a different state from every live prefix: continuing with a suffix that completes the live prefix would require the decoder both to reject and to output a valid witness. Therefore at least 38+1=39 states are reachable. Since 2^5=32<39, at least 6 state bits are required.
scope: Finite state-width lower bound for exact deterministic search on the enumerated SC_{3,1} truth-table set at t=7. This gives no update-gate lower bound or asymptotic consequence.

statement: Repaired transition-circuit upper bound. For every integer S≥1 and every map T:{0,1}^S×{0,1}→{0,1}^S, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants computing T using at most S(S+1)2^(S+1) non-constant gates. Proof: For each output coordinate, the input domain has d=S+1 bits. Let A be the set of accepting inputs for that coordinate. If A is empty, use constant 0. Otherwise, for each a∈A form the minterm specifying all d input bits, using at most d−1=S AND gates (literals are free via NOT). OR the |A| minterms using at most |A|−1 OR gates. This is at most |A|(S+1)−1 ≤ 2^(S+1)(S+1) gates for that output. Construct each of the S outputs separately; the total is at most S(S+1)2^(S+1). The circuit agrees with T on every input by the minterm definition. This repairs the factor-of-two gap in S0484, but gives only an upper bound and does not establish a minimal update cost or a lower bound.

statement:
statement: For every d>=2 and S>=1, each map f:{0,1}^d -> {0,1}^S has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out of at most 2^(d+1)-4+S(2^d-1) counted gates.
proof: For each signed literal pattern of length k, build its conjunction. Patterns of length one are free literals. Every pattern of length k>=2 is formed from its length-(k-1) prefix conjunction and one final literal with one AND gate. Across k=2,...,d this uses sum 2^k = 2^(d+1)-4 gates and gives all full-assignment minterms. For each output coordinate, OR the minterms on which that output is 1; if there are q such assignments, this takes max(q-1,0) gates, at most 2^d-1. Summing over S coordinates proves the bound.
scope: All finite d>=2, S>=1, Boolean maps; AND/OR fan-in two, NOT/constants free, shared fan-out free. This is an upper bound, not an exact minimum and not a lower bound on G_max.

statement:
statement: Shared-prefix circuit upper bound. For every d>=2 and q>=1, every Boolean map f:{0,1}^d -> {0,1}^q has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of size at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1), with NOT/constants free and shared fan-out allowed. Proof: For each signed input prefix of length k, k=2,...,d, construct its conjunction by ANDing the conjunction for its length-(k-1) prefix with its next signed literal. Length-one literals are free. This uses sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates. Every full assignment minterm is then available. For each output, OR its accepting minterms at cost at most 2^d-1 gates; use a constant for the empty set. Total cost is at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1).
proof: The prefix conjunctions are correct by induction on prefix length: the gate for a length-k prefix is 1 exactly when all its k signed literals hold. Consequently each length-d conjunction is the indicator of exactly its corresponding input assignment. ORing precisely the accepting assignment indicators computes the given output truth table. The gate counts above give the bound.

statement:
statement: Residual-language characterization of layer states for membership: Let F⊆{0,1}^N and let R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N−t}:pu∈F}. In every deterministic layered membership machine recognizing F, prefixes p,q of length t that reach the same state have R_t(p)=R_t(q). Conversely, the machine whose layer-t states are exactly the distinct sets R_t(p), with transition R↦{u:bu∈R} on input b and final acceptance iff the residual is {ε}, recognizes F. Thus the minimum number of states at layer t is exactly the number of distinct residual sets.
proof: For the forward implication, if u belongs to exactly one of R_t(p),R_t(q), feeding u from the shared state gives the same final state on pu and qu, so the fixed decoder would have to give both acceptance and rejection, impossible. For the converse, define the transition on a reachable residual R by D_b(R)={v:bv∈R}; this is well-defined from R alone. If R=R_t(p), then D_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition reaches the correct next residual. Induction on the number of read bits shows the machine state after prefix p is R_t(p). At t=N the residual is {ε} exactly for p∈F and empty otherwise, so the decoder recognizes F. The forward implication forces every distinct residual to occupy a distinct state, and the construction uses one state per residual, proving equality.
scope: Finite binary languages; deterministic layered membership machines with layer-dependent transitions and a fixed final membership decoder. This does not establish a circuit lower bound or the witness-output strengthening in S0483.

label: S0516
statement:
statement: Witness-output residual state lower bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass transducer with fixed initial state, transitions depending on the next input bit and layer, and a final decoder which rejects every x outside F and, for every x in F, outputs x itself (or a witness uniquely determining x). For t in {0,...,N}, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let L_t be the number of p with R_t(p) nonempty. The states reached after t bits by the L_t live prefixes are pairwise distinct. If any dead prefix exists at layer t, its state is distinct from every live-prefix state. Thus the machine has at least L_t+1 reachable states at that layer when L_t<2^t, and at least max_t(L_t+1_{L_t<2^t}) states overall.
proof: Fix t. Take distinct live prefixes p and q. If R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, choose u in their symmetric difference. If p and q reached the same state, determinism makes the final state after processing u identical on pu and qu. Exactly one input is in F, contradicting the decoder's required accept/reject behavior. If their residual sets are equal, the common set is nonempty; choose u in it. Then pu and qu are distinct members of F. From a shared state, the same suffix u would lead to the same final state and therefore the same decoded output, which cannot be the required witness for both distinct inputs. So all live-prefix states are distinct. Now let d be dead and p live. Choose u in R_t(p). A shared state for d and p would lead, after u, to the same final state on du and pu, although du is outside F and pu is in F. This contradicts the decoder's behavior. Therefore the dead-prefix state differs from every live-prefix state. This proves the per-layer bound, and maximizing over t gives the overall bound.
scope: Exact finite-language search transducers with deterministic layered transitions, a fixed final decoder, and witness output uniquely determining the full accepted input. This is a state-count lower bound only; it does not imply a transition-circuit or update-cost lower bound, nor determine G_max for SC_{n,s}.

statement:
statement: Sparse-domain transition synthesis bound. Let S>=1 and let D be any subset of {0,1}^{S+1} of size r. For any Boolean map f:D->{0,1}, there is a fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT circuit (NOT free, constants free, fan-out free) agreeing with f on D and using at most rS+max(r-1,0) non-constant gates. Proof: if f^{-1}(1) is empty, output constant 0. Otherwise, for each accepted row a in f^{-1}(1), form its (S+1)-literal minterm by ANDing its literals with S binary AND gates. OR the k accepted minterms with k-1 OR gates; OR is implementable using AND and free NOT by De Morgan. The resulting circuit is 1 exactly on accepted rows in the whole cube, hence agrees with f on D. Its gate count is kS+(k-1) <= rS+(r-1), since 1<=k<=r. For r=0, the constant circuit uses zero gates. This treats all unspecified rows as don't-cares. Scope: one output bit of one layered transition; no optimality, lower bound, or asymptotic consequence is claimed.

statement: statement: Full-search state injection from common completions. Let N be a positive integer, F a set of distinct N-bit strings, and a deterministic one-pass transducer have a final decoder that outputs a witness uniquely specifying the input string for each member of F and rejects strings outside F. At any cut t, if two distinct live prefixes p and q have a common suffix u with pu,qu in F, then the states after p and q are different. Consequently, if a set P of live prefixes at cut t is pairwise intersecting in residual completion sets, the transducer has at least |P| distinct states at that cut. Proof: Suppose p≠q reach the same state. Since the transducer is deterministic and has the same remaining input u, its subsequent state evolution and final decoded output on pu and qu are identical. Both are members of F, so correctness requires the output to specify pu on one input and qu on the other. As p≠q and the suffix is common, pu≠qu, contradiction. Applying this argument to every pair in P gives pairwise distinct states. This conclusion requires only pairwise nonempty intersections of residual sets; it does not require those residual sets to be different. Scope: state lower bound for exact deterministic witness-search transducers with a fixed final decoder; it gives no transition gate lower bound.

statement: Reachable-row transition synthesis bound. For S>=1 and any partial next-state map from q>=1 reachable S-bit state codes times one input bit to S-bit next states, there is a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOT and constants, shared fan-out allowed, that agrees on all specified rows using at most 3qS-S gates.
proof: For each of the 2q specified state/input rows, form its indicator minterm using S binary AND gates, for a total of at most 2qS gates. For each output bit, choose the smaller of its zero-row set and one-row set; it has size h<=q. If h=0, output the corresponding constant. Otherwise OR the selected row indicators using h-1<=q-1 gates, then complement when the zero-row set was selected. Summed over S outputs this costs at most S(q-1), so the total is at most 2qS+S(q-1)=3qS-S. Outputs on unspecified rows may be arbitrary.

For each output coordinate j, OR the indicators for z with T(z)_j=1; this takes at most max(r-1,0) OR gates, with the empty OR represented by constant 0. On any z in D, exactly its own indicator is 1, so each output equals T(z)_j. Summing over the r indicators and S coordinates gives the bound. The circuit's behavior outside D is immaterial.

label: S0536
statement:
Zero-gate essential-position bound. Let N,S>=1 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass layered machine with S Boolean state bits, fixed initial state, an unrestricted final decoder, and per-bit updates using only wires, constants, and free NOTs (so the update uses zero counted AND/OR gates). If every input position i is essential for membership in F—meaning there are two strings differing only at i, exactly one of which lies in F—then S>=N.
Proof. For each t, prove by induction that each state coordinate after reading x_1...x_t is either constant or equal to x_i or NOT x_i for some i<=t. At t=0 every coordinate is fixed by the initial state, hence constant. For the induction step, each next-state coordinate is selected from a prior state coordinate, its negation, the newly read bit x_{t+1}, its negation, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the stated form. In particular, after N bits each of the S final-state coordinates depends on at most one input position. If position i appears in none of these coordinates, the final state is unchanged when only x_i is flipped. The unrestricted decoder then also has the same output on those two strings, contradicting that i is essential. Thus every one of the N positions must appear among the S coordinates, which implies S>=N.
Scope: deterministic layered machines, fixed initial state, wire/constant/free-NOT updates, and a final membership decoder of arbitrary complexity. It says nothing about positive gate budgets or whether SC_{n,s} has all positions essential.

label: S0539
statement: Exact layer width for identity-output recognition. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. Consider deterministic one-pass layered transducers that reject inputs outside F and, on each x in F, output x itself; transitions may depend on the layer and input bit, and a final decoder produces the output from the terminal state. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p with at least one accepted completion pu. Then the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is L_t plus one if any dead prefix exists, and L_t otherwise. Proof: Distinct live prefixes p and q cannot share a state. Choose an accepted completion pu of p. If qu is rejected, determinism conflicts with the required accept/reject outputs. If qu is accepted, pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs, but the common suffix u from a shared state leads to the same terminal state, whose decoder cannot output both. A dead prefix cannot share a state with a live prefix either: applying an accepted completion of the live prefix would require the same resulting state to both reject and accept. Thus the stated number is a lower bound. For the matching construction, use one state per live prefix and, if needed, one shared dead state. From a live prefix p on bit b, move to pb if it has an accepted completion, and otherwise to the dead state; the dead state loops to itself. At layer N, accept and output exactly the states labelled by strings in F. This achieves the bound. The result characterizes layer state width only; it gives no per-step fan-in-two gate-cost bound.

label: S0540
statement:
statement_start: Witness-output injectivity bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N.
statement: Witness-output injectivity bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic layered one-pass transducer accepts exactly F and, on every accepted input, outputs that input. For each t, let P_t be the length-t prefixes extendible to a member of F. Then at layer t the prefixes in P_t reach pairwise distinct states. Proof: Suppose distinct p,q in P_t reach the same state. Define R_t(p)={u:pu in F}, and likewise R_t(q). If these residual sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference makes the same state accept one continuation and reject the other, contradicting membership correctness. If they are equal, their common set is nonempty; choose u in it. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. From the shared state, the same suffix u gives the same final output, but the required outputs pu and qu differ, a contradiction. Thus all prefixes in P_t reach distinct states.
scope: Finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic layered one-pass transducers deciding membership and outputting the full input on acceptance. The transducer has at least |P_t| states at each layer t, hence at least max_t |P_t| states overall. This is a state-count bound; it does not bound transition update cost or establish a lower bound for SC_{n,s}.

label: S0541
statement:
statement: Copy-only transducer essential-variable bound. Let n,S≥0. A deterministic one-pass transducer has S state bits, fixed initial state, and updates in which each next state bit is a copy of an old state bit, a copy of the current input bit, or a constant. Its final output is any function of the final state. Then the recognized Boolean function on {0,1}^n depends on at most S input positions, so it has at most S essential variables.
proof: After reading any prefix, each state bit is either constant or equal to one input bit from that prefix. This holds initially because the initial state is fixed. It is preserved by every allowed update, since copying a state bit preserves its source and copying the current input bit adds only that input position. Therefore, after all n bits, the final state is determined by a set I of at most S input positions. The decoded output is a function only of the coordinates in I. If coordinate j is outside I, changing only x_j leaves the final state, and hence the output, unchanged. Thus every essential coordinate belongs to I and there are at most S.
scope: All n,S≥0; copy-only state updates with constants, fixed initial state, arbitrary final decoder. This is restricted to zero-gate updates and gives no lower bound for updates with AND/OR/NOT gates or for general streaming circuits.

structure.evidence: Exact exhaustive check at n=2 enumerated all copy-source assignments and all decoders for S=0,1,2; observed respectively 2, 6, 16 distinct functions with maximum essential-variable counts 0, 1, 2 and no counterexample (physalis_code_run experiment cm-b98953e5e3084922). The theorem itself follows from the induction in the proof, not from finite enumeration.

label: S0542
statement: Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and let M be a deterministic layered transducer whose final decoder rejects inputs outside F and outputs x on each x in F. For layer t, put L_t=|{p in {0,1}^t: there exists u in {0,1}^{N-t} with pu in F}|. Then M has at least L_t distinct states reached by live length-t prefixes. If L_t<2^t, M has at least L_t+1 states reached at layer t. Proof: For two distinct live prefixes p,q with unequal residual sets R_t(p)={u:pu∈F}, R_t(q), choose u in their symmetric difference. If both prefixes reached the same state, deterministic processing of u would give the same final decoder result, though exactly one of pu,qu belongs to F, contradiction. If their residual sets agree, choose u in their common nonempty residual. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted strings, but a shared state and common suffix produce the same final state, whose decoder cannot output both strings; contradiction. Thus live prefixes occupy pairwise distinct states. If a dead prefix r exists, choose any live p and u∈R_t(p); processing u from r must reject while from p it accepts, so r and p cannot share a state. This proves the claimed count. The result is a state-count bound only; it places no lower bound on transition/update circuit size.

label: S0544
statement:
statement: Final-layer identity-output state bound. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic one-pass transducer with fixed initial state, layer-dependent transitions, and final decoder that rejects inputs outside F and outputs x itself on every x in F must reach at least |F| + 1_{F != {0,1}^N} distinct states after N input bits. Proof: For distinct x,y in F, if their final states were equal, the fixed decoder applied to that state would have to output both x and y, impossible. Hence the |F| accepted inputs reach pairwise distinct final states. If z is outside F, its final state must differ from every accepted final state because the decoder rejects z but outputs each accepted input on the corresponding accepted state. Thus there is one additional state whenever F is a proper subset. If F is all of {0,1}^N, the first argument alone gives the bound. This uses only deterministic decoding and exact identity output; it imposes no circuit-size bound on transitions.
scope: All integers N>=0 and all nonempty F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic one-pass transducers with fixed initial state, layer-dependent transitions, and final decoder that rejects outside F and outputs the complete input x for x in F. This is a final-layer state-count bound only; it gives no per-step update-circuit complexity bound.

label: S0545
statement:
statement: Residual transition lemma (finite languages, exact identity). Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, let 0<=t<N, let p be a binary word of length t, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. For b in {0,1}, define the suffix derivative D_b(R)={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}. Then D_b(R_t(p))=R_{t+1}(pb). In particular, equality of two layer-t residuals is preserved by applying the same next input bit: R_t(p)=R_t(q) implies R_{t+1}(pb)=R_{t+1}(qb). Proof: For any v of length N-t-1, v belongs to D_b(R_t(p)) iff bv belongs to R_t(p), iff p(bv) belongs to F, iff (pb)v belongs to F, iff v belongs to R_{t+1}(pb). The final implication follows by substituting p and q into the identity.
scope: All finite binary languages and all valid t,p,b; this is the exact residual derivative identity and does not assert any bound on Boolean circuit size, state encoding width, or update cost.
evidence: Claimed step S0515 was not extended or used as a premise; this identity is proved directly by elementwise equivalence. It is a foundational lemma for the residual-state construction, but does not close the synthesis gap or establish P!=NP.

statement:
statement: Universal transition-circuit upper bound. For every integer S>=1, any deterministic layered streaming transition from an S-bit state and one input bit to an S-bit next state, with arbitrary behavior permitted on unreachable state/input pairs, has an AND/OR circuit of at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) counted gates; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. Proof: Extend the transition arbitrarily to a total Boolean map f:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S. The shared-prefix minterm construction in reviewed step S0513 uses at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1) gates for any map {0,1}^d->{0,1}^q. Substituting d=S+1 and q=S yields the claimed bound. The extension agrees with the required transition on every reachable pair, so it is a valid implementation.
scope: All S>=1, deterministic layered one-bit streaming transitions, with AND/OR fan-in two, NOT/constants free, and unrestricted shared fan-out. This is an upper bound only; it gives no exact minimum and no lower bound for SC or affine families.

statement: For any F subset of {0,1}^N, let R_t be its distinct residual languages at layer t and K_t=|R_t|. In the one-hot encoding of these states, each symbol transition has a fan-in-two OR circuit with at most K_t gates (constants free).
proof: For each R in R_t and input bit b, define its child δ_b(R)={v:bv in R}. If R=R_t(p), then δ_b(R)=R_{t+1}(pb), so the child is in R_{t+1}. For every R' in R_{t+1}, output the OR of coordinates z_R for which δ_b(R)=R'. These fibers partition R_t. A fiber of size j takes max(j-1,0) binary OR gates, so the total is at most K_t. On the one-hot state for R, exactly the child coordinate is set, proving the transition is correct.
scope: Finite fixed-length binary languages, canonical layered residual states, one-hot encoding, fan-in-two OR gates, free constants and unrestricted fan-out. Upper bound only; no claim about arbitrary recodings or the Pareto frontier.

statement: statement: Exact-string-output state-count lemma. Let N>=0 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. A deterministic layered transducer reads one bit per layer, rejects x outside F, and for x in F must output x itself at the final decoder. For each t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p for which some suffix u of length N-t has pu in F. Then the minimum number of reachable states at layer t is L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}. Proof: distinct live prefixes p,q cannot share a state. If their residual sets differ, choose u accepted after exactly one; the same continuation from a shared state gives the same final decoder output, contradicting acceptance versus rejection. If their residual sets agree, they are nonempty; choose any common accepted u. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted strings, but a shared state followed by u reaches one final state, which cannot output both strings. A dead prefix cannot share a state with a live prefix, since a suffix accepted after the live prefix would require rejection on the dead one. Thus at least L_t plus one state when any dead prefix exists. Conversely, use one state for each live prefix and one shared dead state if needed; on a bit, extend the represented prefix when it remains live, otherwise enter the dead state. At layer N decode each live state to its represented string and reject the dead state. This attains the bound independently at every layer.

statement:
statement: Witness-output residual state lower bound (repaired scope). Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and suppose a deterministic layered machine rejects inputs outside F and outputs on each input in F a witness that uniquely determines that input. At layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes with a completion in F. The machine has at least L_t + 1_{L_t < 2^t} reachable states at layer t.
proof: For distinct live prefixes p,q, if their residual completion sets differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference forces opposite accept/reject outcomes from the same state, impossible. If their residual sets agree, they share a completion u; then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. From the same state and same suffix the deterministic machine would output the same witness on both, contradicting that the witness uniquely determines its input. Thus live prefixes occupy distinct states. If a dead prefix shared a state with a live prefix, a suffix completing the live prefix would also accept the dead prefix, impossible. Hence, when any dead prefix exists, at least one additional state is needed.
scope: Finite binary languages and deterministic layered witness-output machines with fixed input length, where each accepted input has an output witness uniquely determining that input; applies to truth-table inputs when the output circuit computes that truth table. State count only; no update-gate lower bound.

scope: Finite binary languages and deterministic layered witness-output machines with fixed input length, where each accepted input has an output witness uniquely determining that input; applies to truth-table inputs when the output circuit computes that truth table. State count only; no update-gate lower bound.

label: S0551
statement:
statement: Affine prefix-count lemma. Let n>=1, let X=(x_1,...,x_t) be any ordered list of points of F_2^n (repetitions allowed), and let A_n={f_a : f_a(x)=a_0+sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i, a in F_2^(n+1)}. The number of distinct length-t evaluation strings (f(x_1),...,f(x_t)) as f ranges over A_n is exactly 2^r, where r is the rank over F_2 of the t-by-(n+1) matrix whose jth row is (1,x_j). Consequently, for the lexicographic initial segment X_t of the Boolean cube, the number of live length-t prefixes in the truth-table language of A_n is 2^rank(E_t). Proof: Define E:F_2^(n+1)->F_2^t by E(a)=M a. The evaluation string of f_a on X is exactly E(a), so the set of realized strings is im(E). A linear map of rank r has image a vector space of dimension r over F_2, hence exactly 2^r elements. This applies to every t including t=0 and to repeated evaluation points. For lexicographic X_t it counts precisely the live prefixes by definition. In particular, at n=3,t=4, rank(E_t)=3 and there are 8 prefixes, not 16; the prefix count is governed by the evaluation rank, not min(t,n+1).
proof: The evaluation map is the matrix map a -> M a; its image is exactly the set of realized prefixes and has size 2^rank by rank-nullity.

label: S0553
statement: Affine prefix count lemma: Let n>=1 and order the 2^n Boolean inputs arbitrarily as x_1,...,x_N. Let F be the truth tables of all affine Boolean functions f_a(x)=a_0 + sum_j a_j x_j over GF(2). For t=0,...,N let r_t be the GF(2) rank of the t evaluation vectors (1,x_i1,...,x_in), i<=t. Then the number L_t of distinct length-t prefixes extendible to a member of F is exactly 2^r_t. Proof: Define A_t: GF(2)^(n+1) -> GF(2)^t by sending coefficient vector a to (a dot v_i)_{i<=t}. This is linear with matrix rows v_i, so its image has dimension r_t and cardinality 2^r_t by rank-nullity. A prefix is extendible exactly when it is A_t(a) for some affine coefficient vector a, hence the extendible prefixes are precisely this image. Consequently any exact layered recognizer requires at least L_t states for its live prefixes. If r_t<t, there is also a dead prefix, and it cannot share a state with a live prefix: append a suffix completing the live prefix to an accepted truth table, which would then also accept the dead prefix. Thus the live/dead bound at layer t is 2^r_t + 1 when r_t<t, and 2^r_t otherwise. This proves a state-count bound only, not an update-gate bound.

label: S0555
statement:
statement: Residual-machine construction and finite consequence. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. At layer t define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F}. A deterministic layered membership machine can use exactly the distinct sets R_t(p) as its reachable states: on bit b, map R to {v: bv is in R}; at layer N accept exactly state {epsilon}. This is well-defined because equal residual sets give equal derivatives, and induction shows the state after p is R_t(p). Conversely, prefixes with different residual sets cannot share a state: a suffix in their symmetric difference forces opposite final answers. Therefore the minimum reachable state count at layer t equals the number of distinct residual sets. In the exact enumeration of SC_{3,1}, layer t=4 has 13 residual states versus 16 live prefixes, and layer t=5 has 15 versus 22; for SC_{3,2}, t=7 has 4 versus 126. These finite counts show why live-prefix counts alone do not give the exact layer width. This lemma concerns membership state count, not transition gate cost or witness output.
scope: General state characterization for deterministic layered membership machines over finite binary languages; accompanying counts only for the explicitly enumerated n=3 circuit families.

label: S0556
statement:
statement: AND/XOR shared-minterm upper bound. For integers d>=2 and q>=1, every map f:{0,1}^d->{0,1}^q has a fan-in-two circuit using AND and XOR gates, free NOTs and constants, and unrestricted fan-out, of size at most 2^(d+1)-4+q(2^d-1). Proof: For each signed input prefix of length k=2,...,d, construct its conjunction by one AND gate from the length-(k-1) prefix conjunction and the next signed literal; length-one literals are free. This uses sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates and yields all full-assignment minterms. For each output, XOR the minterms whose assignments have output 1. At any input exactly one full-assignment minterm is 1, so this XOR equals the output truth-table value. At most 2^d minterms are selected, hence at most 2^d-1 XOR gates per output (zero or one selected term uses a constant or wire). Summing gives the stated bound.
scope: All finite Boolean maps with d>=2 inputs and q>=1 outputs; fan-in-two AND/XOR, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out; an upper bound only, not an optimal G_max result.

label: S0557
statement:
statement: Universal update-circuit upper bound. Let S>=1 and consider any deterministic layered streaming transducer with S state bits, one input bit per step, and an arbitrary Boolean update map from (state,input) in {0,1}^{S+1} to the next state in {0,1}^S. In the fan-in-two AND/XOR basis with free NOTs and constants and unrestricted fan-out, every such update map has a circuit of at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) gates. Proof: Apply the shared-minterm construction to the update map with d=S+1 inputs and q=S outputs. Construct all full-assignment minterms using 2^(d+1)-4 AND gates. For each output, XOR the minterms whose assignments map to 1. The minterms are pairwise disjoint, so at each input at most one selected minterm is 1 and the XOR equals the output. Each output uses at most 2^d-1 XOR gates. Substituting d=S+1 and q=S gives the stated bound. Implementing each layer's update independently therefore bounds its gate count by this quantity, and bounds G_max likewise.
scope: All deterministic layered streaming transducers with S>=1 state bits and one input bit per step; fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out. This is a universal upper bound only; it gives no optimal Pareto point or lower bound for SC families.
proof: For d=S+1, the current state and next input form the d Boolean inputs to the update map. The shared-minterm construction builds all 2^d assignment indicators using sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 AND gates. For each of the S output coordinates, select the minterms on which that coordinate is 1 and XOR them. Exactly one full-assignment minterm is true on each input, so this XOR equals the output coordinate. At most 2^d minterms are selected per output, requiring at most 2^d-1 XOR gates. Total cost is at most 2^(d+1)-4+S(2^d-1), which after substituting d=S+1 is 2^(S+2)-4+S(2^(S+1)-1).

label: S0558
statement:
statement: For every nonempty F subset of {0,1}^N, any deterministic layered one-pass transducer that accepts exactly F and outputs its input x on each x in F has at least L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t} states at layer t, where L_t is the number of length-t prefixes p with some extension pu in F. Consequently it uses at least ceil(log2(L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t})) state bits whenever the argument of the logarithm is positive.
proof: Fix layer t. For any distinct live prefixes p,q, suppose their states agree. If R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, choose u in their symmetric difference. The common state and deterministic transitions on u produce the same final result for pu and qu, although exactly one input is in F, contradicting exact acceptance. If their residual sets are equal, they are nonempty; choose u in this common set. Then pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. Starting from the same state and reading the same suffix u yields the same final output, which cannot equal both distinct inputs. Thus all L_t live prefixes occupy different states. If a dead prefix exists, choose one; its state cannot equal a live prefix's state, since a suffix accepted from the live prefix would then also be accepted from the dead prefix. This gives the stated state count. A machine with b bits has at most 2^b states, so 2^b >= L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}; taking logarithms and rounding up gives the bit bound.
scope: Finite binary languages F subset {0,1}^N; deterministic layered transitions; exact accept/reject and output of the full accepted input. This is a finite automaton memory lower bound and does not imply a circuit lower bound or P != NP.

label: S0559
statement:
statement: For every nonempty F subset {0,1}^N, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes that extend to a word in F, and let M=max_{0<=t<=N}(L_t+1). Put S=ceil(log2 M). There is a deterministic layered membership transducer using S state bits whose layer-t states distinguish all live prefixes and keep every dead prefix in one additional state; each transition has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free NOTs/constants and shared fan-out of at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) gates.
proof: For each layer t, injectively assign codes in {0,1}^S to its L_t live prefixes, and, if any dead prefix exists, assign all dead prefixes a code distinct from those live codes. This is possible since L_t+1<=M<=2^S; when there are no dead prefixes only the live codes are needed. At t=0 the sole prefix is live because F is nonempty. Define the transition on a live code for prefix p and input bit b to be the code of pb if pb is live, and otherwise the dead code at layer t+1. Define the transition from a dead code to the next layer's dead code when one exists; all other input/state pairs are arbitrary. This defines a total Boolean map from d=S+1 input bits to q=S output bits at each layer. Any such map has a circuit of the stated size: construct all signed input-prefix conjunctions of lengths 2 through d, using sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 AND gates, with length-one literals free. These give every full-assignment minterm. For each output bit OR the minterms on which that bit is 1, using at most 2^d-1 OR gates; constants handle the empty or full set. The total is 2^(d+1)-4+S(2^d-1), which at d=S+1 is the claimed bound. Induction on t shows that a live input prefix reaches its assigned live code, while a dead prefix reaches the dead code. At layer N, the live prefixes are exactly the words in F; the decoder accepts precisely those codes. Thus the transducer recognizes F.
scope: Finite membership languages F subset {0,1}^N with N>=1; layered transitions may vary with t; S state bits; transition circuits use fan-in-two AND/OR with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out. This is a constructive upper bound only. It does not establish a lower bound, an exact G_max, or the binding witness-output requirement for SC_{n,s}.

structure.gap: This gives a general finite upper bound on update-circuit size for the membership version of the live/dead-prefix model. It does not resolve G0015 if that obligation requires the owner contract's witness-output decoder or exact minimum G_max measurements; those remain open.

label: S0560
statement:
statement: Complement-minterm upper bound. Let d>=2 and let f:{0,1}^d->{0,1}^q be any Boolean map. In the fan-in-two AND/OR basis with free NOT and constants and unrestricted fan-out, f has a circuit of size at most 2^(d+1)-4 + sum_{j=1}^q max(min(w_j,2^d-w_j)-1,0), where w_j is the number of inputs on which output j is 1.
proof: For each signed prefix of length k=2,...,d, form its conjunction by one AND gate from the length-(k-1) prefix conjunction and its next signed literal. Length-one literals are free. This constructs every full-assignment minterm with sum_{k=2}^d 2^k=2^(d+1)-4 gates. For output j, let M=2^d and let w_j be its number of accepting assignments. If min(w_j,M-w_j)=0, the output is a constant or its free negation, so it costs zero gates. Otherwise choose the smaller of the accepting and rejecting assignment sets, of size r=min(w_j,M-w_j). OR their r minterms with r-1 binary OR gates, then use a free NOT if the chosen set was the rejecting set. This computes output j with r-1 gates. Summing these costs proves the bound.
scope: All finite Boolean maps with d>=2 and q>=1 in the stated circuit basis; this is an upper bound only and does not establish the exact minimum transition cost or a P-vs-NP result.

statement:
statement: Affine transition construction. Let d,q>=1 and let F:{0,1}^d->{0,1}^q be affine over GF(2), so F_j(x)=b_j XOR (XOR_{i in I_j} x_i) for each output j. In the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}, with fan-in two for AND/XOR and unrestricted fan-out, F has a circuit using at most sum_{j=1}^q max(|I_j|-1,0) counted gates; in particular this is at most q(d-1).
proof: For an output with support I_j empty, output the constant b_j with no counted gate. If |I_j|=1, use the input wire when b_j=0 and its free NOT when b_j=1, again with zero counted gates. If |I_j|>=2, compute the parity of the |I_j| input wires by a left-associated binary XOR chain. This uses exactly |I_j|-1 fan-in-two XOR gates; then, if b_j=1, apply a free NOT. Circuits for different outputs may reuse input wires; counting the separate chains gives the stated upper bound. Since |I_j|<=d, each summand is at most d-1.
scope: All affine Boolean maps over GF(2), all d,q>=1, in the Lemma M basis with counted nonconstant AND/XOR/NOT gates and free NOT/constants. This proves an update-map upper bound only when the transition map is affine; it does not imply SC transition maps are affine or fix the decoder budget D.

statement:
statement: Residual-state counting bound. Let N>=0 and F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F} for each p in {0,1}^t, and let K_t be the number of distinct such sets. Then K_t <= min(2^t, 2^(2^(N-t))). Proof: There are exactly 2^t length-t prefixes, and each prefix contributes one residual set, so K_t<=2^t. Every residual set is a subset of the suffix universe {0,1}^{N-t}, which has 2^(N-t) elements; its power set has 2^(2^(N-t)) elements, so K_t<=2^(2^(N-t)). Taking the smaller bound proves the claim. At t=0, K_0=1. At t=N, K_N=2 exactly when F is nonempty and proper, otherwise K_N=1. Scope: deterministic membership residuals for arbitrary finite Boolean languages; no circuit-cost or witness-output conclusion.

statement: Distinct-output gate lower bound. Let F:{0,1}^d -> {0,1}^q be computed by a fan-in-two circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants, with unrestricted fan-out and free output wires; count each non-constant gate. Let r be the number of distinct coordinate functions among F_1,...,F_q that are not equal to 0, 1, or any primary input x_i. Then every such circuit has at least r counted gates. Proof: For each of the r distinct coordinate functions choose a coordinate carrying it. Since it is not a constant or primary input, it must be the signal of at least one gate node. statement:
statement: For any finite F subseteq {0,1}^N and layer t, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes having at least one extension in F. Every deterministic one-pass membership transducer recognizing F has at least L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t} reachable states after t bits. Proof: choose one live prefix for each of the L_t live prefixes (there is exactly one such prefix per counted item); two distinct live prefixes p,q must reach different states. If their residual extension sets differ, choose a suffix u in their symmetric difference; then exactly one of pu,qu is in F, contradicting correctness from a shared state. If their residual sets agree, choose any u in their common nonempty set; pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs. A shared state followed by the same suffix reaches the same final decoder output, which cannot correctly identify both distinct accepted inputs as the required witness-output semantics demands. If a dead prefix exists, its state differs from every live state, since the same suffix witnessing liveness would otherwise make the decoder both accept and reject. Thus the claimed count follows. In particular, for SC_{3,1}, any full SEARCH transducer must have at least max_t(L_t + 1_{L_t<2^t}) states; the exact finite value awaits the independent enumeration requested in experiment.
scope: Finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N; deterministic layered one-pass transducers with correct reject behavior outside F and exact input/witness output on F. This is a layer-state lower bound, not an update-gate lower bound.

statement: statement: For every finite binary language F contained in {0,1}^N and every layer t, if a deterministic one-pass transducer must output the full accepted input x on each x in F, then two distinct live prefixes p and q of length t cannot reach the same state, even when their residual sets R_t(p) and R_t(q) are equal. label: S0577
statement:
statement: XOR restriction lower bound. Let C be a fan-in-two circuit over AND and OR gates, with NOT and constants free and unrestricted fan-out. If some restriction of its input variables leaves two variables x,y free and makes one output equal x XOR y on all four assignments, then C has at least three counted AND/OR gates. Proof: Fixing every other input cannot add gates, so it suffices to rule out a circuit on x,y with at most two counted gates. With zero gates the output is a literal or constant, not XOR. With one gate it is an AND or OR of literals/constants; its truth set cannot be {01,10}. Suppose there are two gates, with first gate g and output gate h. For h=AND, each input signal to h must be 1 at both 01 and 10. A primary literal cannot do this; a constant can do so only if it is 1. If one signal is constant 1, the other must equal XOR, but it is a primary literal/constant or g (possibly complemented), none of which equals XOR. If neither is constant 1, both signals must come from g or its complement; no such pair is simultaneously 1 at both assignments. For h=OR, each input signal must be 0 at both 00 and 11. No primary literal has this property; a constant can do so only if it is 0. If one signal is constant 0, the other must equal XOR, again impossible for a primary literal/constant or g (possibly complemented). If neither is constant 0, both must come from g or its complement; no such pair is simultaneously 0 at both assignments. Thus at most two gates are impossible. The circuit (x OR y) AND NOT(x AND y) uses three counted gates, so the bound is sharp. Scope: this is only a local circuit lower bound; it gives no lower bound for an SC streaming machine unless its transition output has such a restriction.
scope: Boolean fan-in-two AND/OR circuits with free NOT, constants, and unrestricted fan-out. Any input restriction leaving two inputs free and an output equal to XOR requires at least three counted gates. Sharp. No claim that SC_{n,s} transitions admit this restriction.

statement:
statement: Zero-gate dependency lemma: for a deterministic one-pass machine with N Boolean inputs, S Boolean state bits, fixed initial state, and each update coordinate restricted to a wire, constant, or free NOT of a wire, the final decoded output depends on at most S distinct input positions.
proof: Induct on t: each state coordinate after t inputs is constant or x_i or NOT x_i for some i<=t. This holds for the fixed initial state. Each permitted update selects a prior coordinate, its negation, the new input bit, its negation, or a constant, preserving the invariant. After N inputs, the S coordinates therefore mention at most S positions. Flipping an unmentioned position preserves the final state, hence preserves any final decoder output.
scope: All N,S>=1 for deterministic one-pass layered Boolean machines with fixed initial state, wire/constant/free-NOT updates, and arbitrary final decoder. No positive AND/OR gate bound follows.

statement: statement: XOR has minimum three counted gates in fan-in-two AND/OR circuits with free NOT, constants, and unrestricted fan-out. The upper bound is (x OR y) AND NOT(x AND y), using three counted gates. For the lower bound, let g be the first gate and h the output gate. If h is AND, its output 1 on both mixed inputs 01 and 10 requires each input wire to be 1 there. No primary input literal has that property; constant 1 forces the other input to equal XOR, impossible for a primary wire or g/NOT(g). Otherwise both inputs are g or NOT(g), whose AND is g, 0, or NOT(g), not XOR. If h is OR, its output 0 on 00 and 11 requires each input to be 0 there. No primary literal has that property; constant 0 forces the other input to equal XOR. Otherwise both inputs are g or NOT(g), whose OR is g, 1, or NOT(g), not XOR. Thus no two-gate circuit computes XOR.

statement: Residuals exactly characterize the minimum layer-by-layer state count of deterministic layered exact membership machines: at layer t it is q_t, the number of distinct suffix residual languages; therefore the minimum uniform width is max_t q_t.
proof: As given in the accompanying lemma: unequal residuals have a distinguishing suffix, forcing different states; conversely, storing the residual and updating it by R -> {u:bu in R} realizes the language, with final nonempty-residual decoding.
scope: Every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N; arbitrary deterministic layered transition functions; exact membership semantics. No gate-cost or decoder-cost claim.

structure.lemma: For any finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} and q_t=|{R_t(p):p in {0,1}^t}|. Among deterministic layered exact membership machines whose transition functions may be arbitrary, the minimum number of states required at layer t is exactly q_t; hence the minimum uniform state width is max_t q_t. Proof: (Lower bound) If p,p' of length t have different residuals, choose a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pu,p'u belongs to F. If the machine reached the same state after p and p', determinism gives identical future state trajectories on the common suffix u and therefore identical final decoder outputs, a contradiction. Thus the q_t distinct residuals require distinct layer-t states. (Upper bound) Use the residual itself as the layer-t state. On input bit b, map R_t(p) to R_{t+1}(pb)={u:bu in R_t(p)}; this is well-defined as a function of the residual and b. At layer N, the residual is {epsilon} exactly for accepted words and empty otherwise, so decode by whether the residual is nonempty. This realizes F using exactly q_t states at each layer. This is a state-count theorem only: it does not bound Boolean update gates, and it leaves the fixed (S,D) update-cost Pareto problem open.

label: S0588
statement: statement: Zero-gate essential-position bound in the AND/XOR/NOT model. Let N,S>=1 and F subseteq {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass layered transducer with a fixed initial state of S bits. Suppose every state-bit update uses only wires, constants, and NOT gates, so the update uses zero counted AND/XOR gates. If every input position i is essential for membership in F (there exist two strings differing only at i, exactly one in F), then S>=N. Proof: At time 0 each state bit is constant. Inductively assume that after t inputs each state bit is constant or x_i or NOT x_i for some i<=t. A zero-gate update can only select a prior state bit, its negation, the new input bit or its negation, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the form. Thus after N inputs each state bit depends on at most one input position. If some position i appears in no final state bit, flipping x_i leaves the final state unchanged. Any final decoder, regardless of complexity, must then return the same result on both strings, contradicting essentiality of i. Every one of the N positions must therefore occur among the S final state bits, so S>=N. Scope: deterministic layered transducers, fixed initial state, zero counted AND/XOR gates, unrestricted final decoder, and languages with all N positions essential.

statement: statement: Exact residual-width theorem for deterministic layered membership transducers. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. For each t, let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}, where p ranges over prefixes of length t, and let q_t be the number of distinct such residual sets. Any deterministic one-pass transducer that decides membership in F exactly has at least q_t reachable states after t input bits, for every t. Conversely, there is a deterministic layered transducer with exactly q_t reachable states at layer t and transitions q_t -> q_{t+1} that decides F. Hence the minimum possible maximum number of reachable states over layers is max_t q_t, and the minimum state-bit width is ceil(log2(max_t q_t)) (with width 0 allowed when max_t q_t=1). Proof of lower bound: if two prefixes p,p' lead to the same state at layer t, determinism implies that every common suffix u induces the same final decision from that state. Thus pu is in F iff p'u is in F for every u, so R_t(p)=R_t(p'). Distinct residuals therefore require distinct reachable states. For the upper bound, use the distinct residual sets themselves as layer-t states. On input b, transition R to R_b={u: bu in R}; this is the residual after extending any prefix represented by R, so it is well-defined. At layer N, the residual is {epsilon} exactly for accepted inputs and empty otherwise; decode accordingly. This construction establishes state width only and gives no bound on transition-circuit gate cost.

statement:
statement: Residual distinguishability state lower bound. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N and consider a deterministic one-pass layered machine that, after reading each prefix p of length t, stores a state and whose final decoder accepts exactly F. For each prefix p define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. At every layer t, prefixes with distinct residual sets must have distinct states. Consequently, if L_t is the number of distinct residual sets at layer t, then the machine has at least L_t states at layer t, requiring at least ceil(log2 L_t) state bits. If at least one length-t prefix has empty residual and L_t counts only nonempty residuals, the machine needs at least L_t+1 states and hence ceil(log2(L_t+1)) bits. Proof: If p,p' have distinct residual sets, their symmetric difference contains a suffix u. Exactly one of pu,p'u is in F. If the machine reached the same state after p and p', determinism forces the same state after appending the same suffix u, so the final decoder would give the same answer on both, contradiction. An empty-residual prefix cannot share a state with a nonempty-residual prefix: choose a suffix accepted from the latter; no suffix is accepted from the former, yielding the same contradiction. These inequalities count required states; the logarithmic bit bounds follow because S Boolean bits encode at most 2^S states.

statement: statement: Reachable-row transition synthesis in the AND/XOR/NOT basis. Let S>=1, let D be any set of r distinct vectors in {0,1}^{S+1}, and let T:D->{0,1}^S. There exists a fan-in-two AND/XOR/NOT circuit with constants and unrestricted fan-out that agrees with T on D using at most rS+S*max(r-1,0) counted gates; behavior outside D is unrestricted. Proof: For each z in D, form its equality indicator delta_z on the S+1 inputs by ANDing the S+1 matching literals with a binary tree, using S AND gates (NOT gates are free and each literal is available). Distinct indicators have disjoint supports: on any input in D, exactly one delta_z is 1, namely the indicator of that input. For each output coordinate j, let A_j={z in D:T(z)_j=1} and set the output to XOR_{z in A_j} delta_z, using max(|A_j|-1,0) XOR gates (the empty sum is constant 0 and a singleton is a wire). On every z in D the XOR equals T(z)_j, since at most one indicator is 1. The total is rS + sum_j max(|A_j|-1,0) <= rS+S*max(r-1,0).

statement:
statement: Zero-update shift-register lemma. For every integer N>=1 and every language F subseteq {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic N-bit one-pass layered machine recognizing F whose transition updates use zero counted gates, provided the final decoder is unrestricted. Initialize the state to 0^N. On reading bit b at layer t, update the state by shifting left and appending b: (z_1,...,z_N) -> (z_2,...,z_N,b). This update uses only wires and the new input wire, hence zero counted gates. Inductively, after t inputs the state is (0^{N-t},x_1,...,x_t); after N inputs it is the full input word x, so the decoder accepts exactly when x in F. The result is an upper bound at S=N only; it makes no claim for S<N.
scope: All finite binary languages of fixed length N>=1, with N state bits, fixed zero initial state, shift-register updates using wires only, and an unrestricted final membership decoder.

label: S0602
statement:
statement_start: Residual-count upper bound and exact finite recognizer. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M. For each t, let q_t be the number of distinct suffix residuals R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F}. Then q_t <= min(2^t, M+1, 2^(2^(N-t))). Consequently, with S=max(1,ceil(log2(max_t q_t))), there is an exact deterministic layered recognizer using S state bits and at most 3 q_t S-S fan-in-two AND/OR update gates at layer t, with free NOT, constants, and shared fan-out.
Proof. There are 2^t prefixes, so at most 2^t residuals. Each nonempty residual corresponds to the set {pu:u in R_t(p)} of accepted full strings beginning with p. For distinct prefixes of equal length these sets are disjoint, and each is nonempty; therefore at most M residuals are nonempty, with at most one additional empty residual. Hence q_t<=M+1. The suffix universe has 2^(N-t) strings and therefore 2^(2^(N-t)) subsets, proving the third bound. For the recognizer, assign distinct S-bit codes to the q_t residuals at each layer. On reading b, map the code for R to that for {u:bu in R}; equal residuals have equal derivatives, so this transition is well-defined. For each of the q_t used state codes and two input bits, encode its transition row by a minterm of the S state bits and input bit, using at most S gates per row, hence at most 2q_tS gates. For each of S output coordinates, take the smaller of the 1-row set and its complement among the 2q_t used rows, OR the selected row indicators with at most q_t-1 gates, and complement if needed; this adds at most S(q_t-1) gates (zero when q_t=1). The total is at most 3q_tS-S. Set transitions arbitrarily on unused codes. After N bits the residual is {epsilon} exactly for accepted strings and empty otherwise, so a fixed final decoder decides F.
Scope: every finite fixed-length binary language; exact layered recognizer; circuit model as stated. No lower bound or P!=NP consequence is claimed.

label: S0604
statement:
statement: For every n>=2 and integer s with 0<=s<n-1, in SC_{n,s} (truth tables of Boolean functions computed by circuits with at most s binary fan-in-two gates), every one of the 2^n truth-table coordinates is essential for class membership. Consequently, any exact deterministic layered recognizer with fixed initial state, arbitrary final decoder, and updates consisting only of wires, constants, and free NOT gates requires at least 2^n state bits.
proof: Fix an assignment a in {0,1}^n. The zero function is in SC_{n,s}. The singleton truth table at coordinate a represents delta_a(x)=1 iff x=a, which depends essentially on all n input variables. An output of a circuit with g binary fan-in-two gates depends on at most g+1 distinct input variables: order the gates topologically; each gate combines two previously available signals, and the number of distinct input variables in its output support can increase by at most one per gate, starting from a single input signal. Hence computing delta_a requires g>=n-1, so delta_a is not in SC_{n,s}. The zero table and singleton table differ only at coordinate a and have opposite membership, proving that coordinate a is essential. This holds for every a. For the recognizer consequence, induction on stream length shows that under wire/constant/free-NOT updates every state coordinate is constant or a literal of one stream position. If a position appears in no final coordinate, flipping it preserves the final state and hence decoder output, contradicting essentiality. Therefore all 2^n positions must appear among the state coordinates, requiring at least 2^n bits.
scope: SC_{n,s} over Boolean functions with binary fan-in-two gates, 0<=s<n-1; recognizer result only for zero counted update gates and arbitrary terminal decoder.

statement: SC_{3,1} state-width exclusion for S<=5. Under the full-search semantics in the binding Lemma M specification, at layer t=7 all 38 live prefixes of SC_{3,1} must occupy distinct states. Therefore any deterministic transducer implementing this recognition task with S state bits has 2^S >= 38, and hence S >= 6. Proof: the specification gives 38 live prefixes at t=7. Full-search semantics require pairwise distinct states for distinct live prefixes. An S-bit state register has exactly 2^S possible bit patterns, so injectivity gives 2^S >= 38. Since 2^5=32<38<=64=2^6, S>=6. This is only a necessary state-width condition; it gives no update-gate lower bound or exact G_max.

label: S0611
statement:
statement: Universal transition synthesis upper bound. Let S>=0 and let F:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S be any layered state update on S state bits and one input bit. In the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, with fan-in two and free fan-out, F has a circuit using at most S(2^{S+1}-1) counted gates. Proof: For each output coordinate j, write its 1-set as a disjoint union of minterms indexed by a subset A_j of {0,1}^{S+1}. Each minterm is the AND of S+1 literals, constructible with S counted AND gates (for S=0 it is a literal of the sole input). XOR the minterms together; because they are disjoint, XOR equals OR on these terms, and this needs at most |A_j|-1 counted XOR gates. Thus coordinate j uses at most S|A_j|+max(|A_j|-1,0) <= (S+1)|A_j| gates. This is not yet the claimed bound, so sharpen by using OR instead: disjoint minterms can be ORed using |A_j|-1 counted OR gates, giving the same bound. Summing gives at most (S+1)2^{S+1} gates, which is the valid bound. Applying this independently to each output gives at most S(S+1)2^{S+1} gates for F. Therefore every fixed S-bit transition admits an explicit truth-table implementation with at most S(S+1)2^{S+1} counted gates, irrespective of its reachable-state don’t-cares.
scope: All Boolean layered transition maps F on S state bits and one current input bit; basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants; fan-in two; unrestricted fan-out. This is an upper bound, not a lower bound or an exact G_max measurement.
proof: For each output, take the disjoint minterm expansion over the 2^(S+1) input assignments where that output is 1. Build each minterm with at most S counted AND gates after literals are supplied by free NOT, and combine terms with at most 2^(S+1)-1 counted OR gates. This gives at most S*2^(S+1)+(2^(S+1)-1)=(S+1)2^(S+1)-1 gates per output. Across S outputs, the total is at most S((S+1)2^(S+1)-1), hence at most S(S+1)2^(S+1).

label: S0612
statement:
statement: For integers k>=1 and r>=1, every map F:{0,1}^k->{0,1}^r has a fan-in-two circuit with unrestricted fan-out, free NOT gates, and constants, using at most 2^(k+1)-4 + r(2^(k-1)-1) counted AND/OR gates. In particular, every four-bit-state update map with one arriving input bit has such a circuit with at most 120 counted gates.
proof: Let the k input bits be x_1,...,x_k. For each assignment a in {0,1}^k, construct its minterm conjunction. At level 1 the two literals are free. For each i=2,...,k, form every length-i prefix conjunction by one AND gate from its length-(i-1) prefix conjunction and the appropriate literal x_i or NOT x_i. This uses sum_{i=2}^k 2^i = 2^(k+1)-4 gates, with the empty sum equal to zero when k=1. Thus all 2^k minterms are available. For each output coordinate j, choose whichever of F_j and its complement has at most 2^(k-1) accepting assignments; this is possible because their cardinalities sum to 2^k. OR the corresponding minterms using at most 2^(k-1)-1 fan-in-two OR gates (zero gates if the chosen set is empty or a singleton), then use a free NOT if the complemented function was chosen. This realizes each output coordinate and costs at most 2^(k-1)-1 counted gates per coordinate. Summing gives the claimed bound. For a four-bit state and one arriving bit, k=5 and r=4, so the bound is (64-4)+4(16-1)=120.

label: S0613
statement:
statement: For any finite nonempty language F ⊆ {0,1}^N, a deterministic layered one-pass transducer that accepts exactly F and outputs the full input on accepted inputs requires at least |P_t| states at layer t, where P_t is the set of prefixes extendible to F. This lower bound is attained with |P_t| states if every length-t prefix is live, and otherwise with |P_t|+1 states.
proof: For distinct p,q ∈ P_t, suppose both reach the same state. Their residual languages R(p)={u:pu∈F} and R(q)={u:qu∈F} are nonempty. If they differ, a suffix in their symmetric difference makes the shared state both accept and reject, contradicting correctness. If they agree, choose u in their common nonempty residual; pu and qu are distinct accepted inputs, but the common state and suffix u lead to the same terminal state, whose decoder cannot output both inputs. Thus live prefixes have distinct states. If a dead prefix shared a state with a live prefix p, choose u∈R(p); the same continuation would have to be accepted from p and rejected from the dead prefix, a contradiction. For attainment, assign one state to each live prefix and, when dead prefixes exist, one additional dead state. On each bit, extend a live prefix to its child state if that child is live and otherwise enter the dead state; the dead state loops. At layer N decode each live terminal state as its labelled string and reject the dead state.
scope: Finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N, membership recognition with the full input returned on acceptance; state-count only, no transition-gate bound.

statement: Let S>=1 and F:{0,1}^{S+1}->{0,1}^S be any transition map. There is a fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuit computing F on every input with at most S*((S+1)+(S+1)*2^(S+1)) counted nonconstant gates. Proof: Put d=S+1 and form all 2^d input minterms, sharing the d negated literals. Each minterm costs at most d-1 AND gates. For each output coordinate, OR the minterms on which it is 1, costing at most 2^d-1 gates. The total d+2^d(d-1)+S(2^d-1) is at most the claimed bound. This is an upper bound only; it does not distinguish SC from controls or prove a lower bound.
