statement: statement: One-hot transition lemma. Let Q_t and Q_{t+1} be finite nonempty state sets of sizes q and r, and let δ:Q_t×{0,1}→Q_{t+1} be any total transition map. Encoding each state as its one-hot indicator vector, the next-layer one-hot vector is computed by a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit with free constants and unrestricted fan-out using at most 4q gates. Proof: For each u∈Q_t form the two edge indicators e_{u,0}=x_u∧¬b and e_{u,1}=x_u∧b, using 2q AND gates (NOT is free). For each v∈Q_{t+1}, output y_v as the OR of the edge indicators e_{u,b'} for which δ(u,b')=v. If there are d_v such indicators, this takes max(d_v−1,0) binary OR gates, with the empty case implemented by constant 0. Since δ is total, Σ_v d_v=2q, and therefore Σ_v max(d_v−1,0)≤2q. Total size is at most 4q. On every valid one-hot input x_u and arriving bit b, exactly the indicator for δ(u,b) is 1, so the outputs are exactly the next state's one-hot encoding. Scope: one transition layer of a finite deterministic automaton; this is an upper bound only, and does not cover witness-output decoding or prove an exact minimum for SC_{3,1}.

structure.evidence: Direct construction and gate count: 2q shared edge-indicator AND gates, followed by at most 2q OR gates because the transition map has exactly 2q labelled edges. label: S0715
statement: statement: Sharpened one-hot transition upper bound. Let Q and Q' be finite sets with |Q|=q>=1 and |Q'|=r>=1, and let delta:Q×{0,1}->Q' be total. For v in Q', let d_v=|{(u,b):delta(u,b)=v}|. Under one-hot encoding, with fan-in-two AND/OR gates, free NOT/constants, and unrestricted fan-out, the next one-hot vector is computable using at most 2q + sum_{v in Q'} max(d_v-1,0) gates. Proof: For each u form e_(u,0)=x_u AND NOT b and e_(u,1)=x_u AND b, using 2q AND gates. For each v, OR its d_v incoming indicators using max(d_v-1,0) gates; if d_v=0 output constant 0. On a valid one-hot input and either value of b, exactly one edge indicator is 1, so exactly the output coordinate indexed by delta(u,b) is 1. Summing gives the stated count. Since sum_v d_v=2q, this is at most 4q and is strictly smaller whenever some output coordinate has multiple incoming edges. This is a representation-dependent transition upper bound only; it does not determine the minimum over encodings or satisfy a search-witness decoder requirement.

statement:
statement: Residual-language state theorem. Let N>=0 and F⊆{0,1}^N. In any deterministic layered recognizer reading one bit per layer, prefixes p,q of length t that reach the same state must have equal residuals R_t(p)={u∈{0,1}^{N-t}:pu∈F}. Conversely, there is a recognizer using exactly K_t states at layer t, where K_t is the number of distinct residuals. Proof: If p and q reach the same state, determinism makes every common continuation u have the same final acceptance outcome, so pu∈F iff qu∈F; hence their residuals are equal. For the converse, use one state per distinct residual. On bit b, transition R_t(p) to R_{t+1}(pb). This is well-defined: equality of R_t(p) and R_t(q) implies for every suffix v that bv∈R_t(p) iff bv∈R_t(q), hence v∈R_{t+1}(pb) iff v∈R_{t+1}(qb). At layer N, accept exactly the state whose residual is {empty}. This recognizes F with K_t states at each layer.
scope: All finite binary languages F⊆{0,1}^N, N≥0; deterministic layered membership recognition with arbitrary layer-dependent transitions and final decoder. State count only; no bound on transition circuit complexity.

label: S0717
statement:
statement: Zero-gate projection lemma. In a layered streaming transducer with fixed initial state, if every update uses zero counted gates in the basis AND, XOR, NOT, constants, and wires, then after t input bits each state coordinate is constant or a literal of one of those t input bits. Consequently, if live prefixes at layer t must have distinct states, some set of at most S input positions separates the live-prefix family by coordinate projection.
proof: At time zero every state coordinate is fixed, hence constant. With zero counted gates, each output coordinate of an update can only be a constant, a wire from a prior state coordinate or the new input bit, or the complement of one such wire. Inductively, if every coordinate at time t is constant or a signed copy of one of x_1,...,x_t, every coordinate at time t+1 is constant or a signed copy of one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. Thus the state vector at layer t is determined by the set I_t of input positions used by its nonconstant coordinates. If two live prefixes agree on I_t, their states agree. Pairwise distinct live-prefix states therefore imply that restriction to I_t is injective on the live-prefix family.
scope: Finite layered streaming transducers with fixed initial state, zero counted gates in every update, free NOT/constants and wires, and pairwise distinct states for live prefixes at each layer. No claim about positive gate counts or a P-vs-NP lower bound.

label: S0784
statement:
statement: Layer-dependent support lemma. Consider a layered transducer with a fixed initial state and S state bits. At update i (1<=i<=t), suppose each next-state bit is computed by a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with at most G_i gates, with NOTs/constants free and unrestricted fan-out. Then each state bit after t updates depends on at most P_t=∏_{i=1}^t(G_i+1) distinct input positions. Consequently, if all 2^t prefixes are live and have pairwise distinct states, then t<=S P_t.
proof: Let A_i be the union of input positions on which any state bit after i updates depends, and let P_i=∏_{j=1}^i(G_j+1), with P_0=1. Initially A_0 is empty. At update i, each output bit is a circuit with at most G_i binary gates over the S old state bits and the new input bit. Its output has at most G_i+1 distinct primary input wires in its ancestor graph: starting from one output and tracing backwards, each binary gate can add at most one new wire to the connected ancestor subgraph. Thus it depends on at most G_i+1 members of the old-state/input wire set. Each old state wire depends only on positions in A_{i-1}; the new input wire contributes at most one additional position. More carefully, the support of an output is contained in the union of at most G_i+1 supports, each old-state support having size at most P_{i-1} and the new input support size one. Since P_{i-1}>=1, this union has size at most (G_i+1)P_{i-1}=P_i. This proves the bound by induction. Across S state bits, the union of their supports has size at most S P_t. If S P_t<t, some input coordinate is absent from every state bit; flipping that coordinate leaves the state unchanged. This contradicts pairwise distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. Hence t<=S P_t.
scope: Finite layered deterministic transducers; fixed initial state; S state bits; update i uses at most G_i fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out; at the stated layer all 2^t prefixes are live and SEARCH semantics requires distinct states.

label: S0785
statement:
statement: Zero-gate coordinate characterization. In a layered binary transducer with fixed initial state, free wires, NOTs, and constants, and no counted gates per update, each state bit at layer t is a constant or a literal of one of the first t input coordinates. Consequently, the live prefixes at layer t can be assigned distinct states by a zero-gate update history if and only if some set of input coordinates distinguishes every pair of live prefixes.
proof: Induct on t. At t=0 all state bits are constants. At each update, an output bit is a wire from a preceding state bit or the incoming bit, optionally negated, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the form. Thus every state bit at layer t is constant or a signed copy of one of the first t coordinates. The state is therefore a function only of the selected coordinates, so if two live prefixes agree on them they collide. Conversely, given a coordinate set distinguishing every pair, assign state wires to store those coordinates as they arrive (using free wiring and constants), with their signs chosen arbitrarily; the resulting state vectors distinguish all live prefixes. This is a layerwise encoding characterization; consistency of a single fixed transducer across all layers additionally requires choosing the coordinate set schedule compatibly over time.
scope: Finite binary prefix sets at a fixed layer; zero counted gates, free wires/NOTs/constants, fixed initial state. The necessity holds for any such transducer. The sufficiency is for a specified layer encoding and coordinate-storage schedule; it does not assert dead-state separation or a global SC_{n,s} machine.

label: S0786
statement: Lemma (bounded-gate support). Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates per update, with free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out. For every t>=1, each state bit after t updates depends on at most (G+1)^(t-1) input positions. If every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^(t-1). Proof: after update 1, each state output depends on at most the single input bit. For any later output, its ancestor circuit has at most G+1 distinct primary signals: a connected fan-in-two circuit with at most G gates. Each signal is either the incoming bit or a prior state bit. If prior state bits depend on at most B input positions, every primary signal has support at most B, since B>=1 and the incoming bit has support one. Thus the new output support is at most (G+1)B. Induction gives the per-bit bound. Injectivity on all 2^t prefixes implies every input position affects some state bit; otherwise flipping that position leaves the state unchanged. The union of supports of S state bits covers t positions and has size at most S(G+1)^(t-1), proving the inequality. Scope: fixed initial state, layered deterministic binary-input transducer, at most G fan-in-two gates per update; no conclusion about SC-family G_max or P versus NP.

statement:
statement: Gate-free width bound for SC_{3,1}. In any layered transducer with a fixed initial state, S binary state bits, and updates using only free wires, NOTs, and constants, if the layer-t live prefixes must have distinct states, then |P_t| <= 2^S. In particular, using the supplied exact profile |P_7|=38 for SC_{3,1}, every such gate-free machine needs S>=6.
proof: At layer t the transducer has a state in {0,1}^S for each live prefix, by determinism from the fixed initial state. Distinct-state SEARCH semantics makes the map from P_t into {0,1}^S injective. Since the codomain has exactly 2^S elements, |P_t|<=2^S. For SC_{3,1}, the supplied profile gives |P_7|=38. Since 2^5=32<38, S cannot be at most 5; hence S>=6. The gate restriction is not needed for the counting inequality itself, so in particular it holds for gate-free machines.
scope: Finite SEARCH-semantics layered transducers at a specified layer. The SC_{3,1} corollary uses the supplied exact n=3,s=1 truth-table-prefix profile at t=7. This is a state-width lower bound only; it gives no positive gate lower bound and no asymptotic P versus NP consequence.

statement: Bounded-gate support bound (independent derivation). Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates in each update; wires, NOTs, and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. For any t, each state coordinate after t updates depends on at most (G+1)^t input positions. If all 2^t prefixes are live and pairwise distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^t.
proof: For an update with g<=G binary gates, an output's ancestor circuit depends on at most g+1 primary inputs: tracing backward from the output, each binary gate can add at most one new input, while wires and NOTs add none. statement:
statement: Layered support bound (necessary condition). Let a deterministic layered transducer have a fixed initial state, S Boolean state bits, and at each update a Boolean circuit with at most G>=1 fan-in-two gates; NOTs and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. If every length-t input prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must occupy distinct states, then t <= S*((G+1)^t-1)/G. Proof: For each state bit after j updates, let its support be the set of among the first j input positions on which it functionally depends, and let M_j be the maximum support size over the S bits. M_0=0. In a fan-in-two circuit with at most G gates, the ancestor circuit of one output has at most G+1 distinct primary inputs: its underlying ancestor graph is connected, and adding each binary gate introduces at most one new leaf; an output bypassing gates has support at most one. Those primary inputs are previous state bits and possibly the newly read bit. Thus the next output support is contained in a union of at most G+1 previous-state supports, together with at most the singleton new position, so M_{j+1} <= (G+1)M_j+1. Induction gives M_t <= sum_{i=0}^{t-1}(G+1)^i = ((G+1)^t-1)/G. If two prefixes differ only at position i and i is absent from every final state-bit support, their resulting states agree; injectivity on all 2^t prefixes therefore forces every one of the t positions into the union of state-bit supports. That union has size at most S*M_t, yielding the inequality. This is a necessary condition only and does not imply an asymptotic lower bound for SC_{n,s} or the full Lemma M model.
scope: Finite layered Boolean transducers with the specified gate basis and full-live, pairwise-distinct prefix layer; all integers S>=1, G>=1, t>=0.

statement: Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and at layer t call a prefix p live when it has at least one completion in F. Write R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}, and let K_t be the number of distinct nonempty residuals R_t(p) among live prefixes. If at least one length-t prefix is dead, then the minimum number of distinct states in any deterministic layer-t membership machine that assigns distinct states to distinct live residuals and requires every dead prefix state to be disjoint from all live states is exactly K_t+1. If no prefix is dead, the minimum is K_t. Proof: distinct live residuals must have distinct states, giving at least K_t live states; when a dead prefix exists, its state cannot equal any live state, giving at least K_t+1. Conversely, assign one state to each distinct nonempty residual and, when present, one additional state to the empty residual. This assignment satisfies both requirements. For the layered residual machine, the transition on state R and bit b is the residual {v:bv in R}; the empty residual maps to itself, so this assignment is transition-consistent at every layer.

statement:
statement: For any finite fixed-length language F subseteq {0,1}^N, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes extendible to a word in F, and let delta_t be 1 iff some length-t prefix is not extendible. Every deterministic layered SEARCH machine that accepts exactly F and gives distinct states to distinct live prefixes at layer t, while separating live from dead prefixes, needs at least L_t+delta_t states at layer t. Thus S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t+delta_t)) state bits. Proof: The L_t live prefixes occupy distinct states by SEARCH semantics. If delta_t=1, a dead prefix must occupy a state different from every live prefix, adding one more state. If delta_t=0, the live-prefix count already gives the bound. An S_t-bit register has at most 2^S_t states. The bound is tight as an occupancy bound at a single layer: assign separate codes to each live prefix and, if present, one additional code to all dead prefixes. This construction makes no claim about compatibility of codes across layers, gate cost, or decoder cost.
scope: Every finite F subseteq {0,1}^N, each layer 0<=t<=N, deterministic layered SEARCH semantics with live prefixes pairwise state-distinct and live/dead separation; update logic unrestricted.

statement: Let a layered Boolean transducer start in a fixed state and update S state bits from the current S state bits and one new input bit. proof: Define the support of a Boolean function of the input prefix as the set of coordinates on which it functionally depends. Initially every state bit has empty support, so M_0=0. Thus the output depends on at most G+1 primary inputs among the old state bits and the newly read input. If it uses k old state bits and the new input indicator e in {0,1}, then k+e<=G+1. Therefore all t coordinates occur in the union of the S supports, whose size is at most S M_t; hence t<=S M_t.

statement: Support-growth lemma for bounded-gate layered transducers. Let a deterministic layered transducer start in a fixed state and update S Boolean state bits from the previous state and one input bit per layer. Each output is computed by a single-output fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with at most G binary gates, with NOTs and constants free and fan-out unrestricted, where G>=1. Set M_0=0 and M_{t+1}=(G+1)M_t+1. proof: A single output circuit with g binary gates has at most g+1 distinct primary source wires in its ancestor circuit: if g>0, begin at the output gate and add ancestor gates, each of which can introduce at most one new source; if g=0, the output is a constant or one wire. Assuming each old state bit depends on at most M_t input coordinates, the new output depends only on the union of at most k old supports and, if e=1, the current input. Its support size is at most k M_t+e <= (G+1)M_t+1. Induction yields M_t=1+(G+1)+...+(G+1)^(t-1)=((G+1)^t-1)/G. If some input coordinate were absent from every state-bit support at layer t, flipping that coordinate would leave the state unchanged, contradicting pairwise distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. Therefore t is at most the sum of the S support sizes, which is at most S M_t.

statement: Exact residual-state lower bound with dead-prefix condition. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N, let L_t be the number of length-t prefixes p having at least one completion pu in F, and let d_t indicate whether at least one length-t prefix has no completion in F. In any deterministic layered membership machine whose state after prefix p determines acceptance for every suffix, the number of distinct states at layer t is at least L_t+d_t. Consequently its state width S_t satisfies S_t >= ceil(log2(L_t+d_t)); when no dead prefix exists, this is ceil(log2 L_t), and when one exists, it is ceil(log2(L_t+1)). Proof: For each live prefix p define its residual R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}:pu in F}. If two live prefixes have different residuals, some suffix u belongs to exactly one residual, so the machine must be in different states after those prefixes, since the same state followed by u must have the same acceptance outcome. Thus every distinct live residual requires a distinct state; moreover two live prefixes with equal residual need not be distinct for this bound, so refine L_t here to K_t, the number of distinct nonempty residuals. If a dead prefix exists, its residual is empty, which differs from every live residual and requires one further state. Hence the exact justified bound is K_t+d_t states, and therefore S_t>=ceil(log2(K_t+d_t)). Scope: deterministic layered exact membership machines with suffix-independent terminal acceptance; no assumptions on update gates or decoder implementation. This is a state lower bound only, not a gate-cost or P versus NP result.

statement:
statement: For any d Boolean primary inputs, let a multi-output circuit use constants, free NOT gates, unrestricted fan-out, and G nonconstant fan-in-two AND/XOR gates. Identify Boolean functions up to complementation. Exclude the classes of constants and primary input literals (each input and its complement). Then at most G distinct remaining classes can occur among the outputs; consequently any required output list containing r such classes needs at least r nonconstant gates.
Proof: Topologically order the G counted gates. label: S0799
statement: statement: Universal finite synthesis bound for a layered residual machine. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, let K=max_t K_t where K_t is the number of distinct nonempty residual sets at layer t, and let S=max(1,ceil(log2 K)). There is a deterministic layered membership machine using S bits per layer plus one dead code, whose transition at each layer is computable by at most 2^(S+2)-4 + S(2^(S+1)-1) fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, with NOTs, constants, and fan-out free. Proof: At each layer, injectively assign the at most K_t nonempty residuals to S-bit codes, reserving any unused code as dead when one exists; if all 2^S codes are occupied and a dead prefix is reachable, the stated state allocation is insufficient, so instead use S'=ceil(log2(K+1)) bits. For each layer and input bit, define the next code on every reachable live code as the code of its residual derivative, or the reserved dead code when the derivative is empty, and map dead to itself. Extend this partial map arbitrarily to all (S'+1)-bit inputs. Any Boolean function of d=S'+1 inputs with q=S' outputs has a shared-minterm implementation: form all 2^d minterms using at most 2^(d+1)-2d-2 gates, then XOR the selected minterms for each output using at most q(2^d-1) gates. Thus each update has at most 2^(S'+2)-2(S'+1)-2 + S'(2^(S'+1)-1) gates. The terminal decoder tests whether the residual is {epsilon}. Induction using the residual derivative proves exact recognition of F. Scope: finite binary languages, fan-in-two AND/XOR basis, free NOT/constants, unrestricted fan-out; this is an upper bound only and gives no optimal Pareto point for SC families.

statement:
statement: Zero-gate coordinate criterion: for a finite fixed-length language F, a zero-gate layered SEARCH transducer of width S exists iff there are coordinate sets A_t subseteq [t], |A_t|<=S, A_0=empty, A_{t+1} subseteq A_t union {t+1}, whose projections distinguish all distinct live prefixes and every live prefix from every dead prefix at each t.
proof: Only if: Induction on t shows every state bit is a constant or a literal of one of the first t input bits, since this holds at the fixed initial state and each zero-gate update copies, negates, or constants a prior bit or the new bit. Let A_t be the coordinates represented by the nonconstant state wires; then |A_t|<=S and A_{t+1} subseteq A_t union {t+1}. Equal projections give equal states. SEARCH requires distinct live prefixes to differ in state. A live and dead prefix must also differ, since a live prefix has an accepting continuation and a dead prefix has none, and equal states followed by the same continuation yield equal outputs. Conversely, given such A_t, store each retained coordinate in a wire, filling unused wires with constants. The nesting condition permits each update wire to copy a retained coordinate, copy or negate the new input, or be constant, so costs zero gates. The separation condition gives SEARCH correctness; an unrestricted terminal decoder accepts exactly F. This is a finite structural lemma and implies no positive gate lower bound.
scope: Finite binary languages of fixed length; specified zero-gate basis with free NOT/constants and unrestricted fan-out; terminal decoder unrestricted.

label: S0802
statement:
statement: Corrected bounded-gate support bound. Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, fixed initial state, one new binary input bit per update, unrestricted fan-out, and at most G fan-in-two AND/XOR gates per update, with NOTs/constants free. Put M_0=0 and M_t=((G+1)^t-1)/G for G>=1, and M_t=t for G=0. After t updates, each state bit is a Boolean function of at most M_t of the first t input positions. If every length-t prefix is live and distinct live prefixes must reach distinct states, then t<=S M_t.
proof: Induct on t. Initially every state bit is constant, so its support is empty. At one update, the ancestor circuit of any output has at most G gates. In a fan-in-two circuit, its connected ancestor graph has at most G+1 distinct primary inputs: start at the output and expose ancestors; each binary gate can introduce at most one additional distinct input beyond the first. Thus the next state bit depends on at most G+1 of the previous S state bits and the new input bit. If each previous state bit depends on at most M_t original positions, the union of their supports together with the new position has size at most (G+1)M_t+1. The recurrence M_{t+1}=(G+1)M_t+1 with M_0=0 solves to ((G+1)^t-1)/G for G>=1; when G=0 it gives M_t=t. For injectivity, every one of the t input positions must occur in the support of at least one state bit: otherwise flipping that position while fixing all others leaves every state bit unchanged, contradicting distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes. The union of S supports has size at most S M_t, hence t<=S M_t.
scope: Finite layered deterministic transducers under the stated AND/XOR, free-NOT, fan-in-two model; full layer consists of all 2^t live prefixes with SEARCH injectivity. This is a support bound only; it does not imply a positive G lower bound when M_t is large or apply directly to the SC_{n,s} family without checking its live-prefix profile.

statement:
statement: For any layered deterministic transducer with S state bits, fixed initial state, and at most G fan-in-two gates per update (NOTs/constants free, unrestricted fan-out), after t input updates each state bit depends on at most (G+1)^t input positions. If all 2^t prefixes are live and must occupy distinct states, then t <= S(G+1)^t.
proof: For one output of an update circuit with g<=G binary gates, retain only its ancestor DAG. Every retained gate has a path to the output, so the underlying ancestor graph is connected; it has g binary-gate vertices and at most g+1 distinct primary-input leaves, since each binary gate adds at most one leaf to a connected graph. Unary NOT gates and constants add no input positions. Thus each next-state bit depends on at most G+1 previous-state bits or the current input bit. Initially every state bit has empty input support. Inductively, after t updates its support is contained in the union of at most G+1 supports from the preceding layer, each of size at most (G+1)^(t-1), hence has size at most (G+1)^t. Across S state bits, at most S(G+1)^t input positions affect the state. If fewer than t positions occur, flipping an absent position preserves the state, contradicting injectivity across all 2^t prefixes. Therefore t<=S(G+1)^t.

statement:
statement: Sharper support recurrence for layered transducers. Let S>=1 and G>=0 be integers. Consider a deterministic layered transducer with S state bits, fixed initial state, one incoming Boolean input per update, at most G fan-in-two gates per update-output circuit, free NOT/constants, and unrestricted fan-out. After t>=0 updates, each state bit depends on at most B_t input positions, where B_0=0 and B_t=G B_(t-1)+1; hence B_t=sum_{j=0}^{t-1}G^j. If all 2^t prefixes are live and must have pairwise distinct states, then t<=S B_t.
Proof: Fix an output of the update circuit and retain its ancestor DAG. If it contains g<=G binary gates, the number of distinct primary-input leaves is at most g+1: the underlying ancestor graph is connected, and each binary gate can increase the number of leaves by at most one. At most one of those leaves is the current input bit, so at most g<=G leaves are previous-state bits. Each such bit depends on at most B_(t-1) earlier input positions by induction. The current input contributes at most one additional position. Thus the output support has size at most G B_(t-1)+1=B_t. The base case is the fixed initial state, with empty support. Taking the union over S state bits gives at most S B_t input positions affecting the state. Injectivity on all 2^t prefixes requires every position among the t bits to affect the state: otherwise flipping an absent position preserves the state. Therefore t<=S B_t.

statement:
statement: Zero-gate wire lemma. In a deterministic layered transducer with S>=1 state bits, fixed initial state, unrestricted free fan-out, and zero paid update gates (so each next-state coordinate is a constant or a wire from one prior-state coordinate or the current input bit), each state coordinate after any t updates depends on at most one of the t input positions. Consequently, if all 2^t length-t prefixes are live and require pairwise distinct states, then S>=t. Proof: Induct on t. Initially each coordinate is constant and has empty support. At an update, a constant has empty support; a wire from a prior coordinate inherits its support; a wire from the current input has singleton support. Thus each coordinate's support has size at most one. If S<t, the union of the S coordinate supports omits a stream position, so flipping that position leaves the whole state unchanged, contradicting pairwise distinctness. This is a restricted-class exact statement and does not imply a positive paid-gate lower bound for SC_{n,s}.
proof: Induct on the number of updates. At time zero every coordinate is constant, hence has empty support. Suppose each coordinate at time t depends on at most one of the first t input positions. A zero-gate coordinate at time t+1 is either constant, a prior-state coordinate, or the incoming bit. Its support is respectively empty, inherited (and still size at most one), or the singleton containing position t+1. Therefore every coordinate at t+1 has support size at most one. If all 2^t prefixes are live and pairwise distinct states are required, the union of the supports of the S coordinates must contain every one of the t input positions: otherwise flipping an omitted bit leaves every coordinate, and thus the state, unchanged. Since this union has size at most S, t<=S.

NOT is excluded unless counted as paid; free fan-out, and full-search pairwise-distinct live-prefix semantics. The conclusion applies only to a full live layer of depth t.

statement:
statement: Zero-gate support lemma. Let a layered deterministic transducer have S state bits, a fixed initial state, and per-layer updates using only wires, constants, and free NOT gates (equivalently, each next-state coordinate is a constant or a literal of one current-state coordinate or the incoming bit). After t input bits, each state coordinate is a constant or a literal of at most one of those t input bits. If all 2^t prefixes at depth t are live and distinct live prefixes must have distinct states, then t <= S.
proof: Induct on t. At t=0 all coordinates are constants because the initial state is fixed. Thus after t steps the state vector depends on at most S distinct input positions. If t>S, at least one of the t positions occurs in no coordinate; flipping that position leaves the state unchanged. statement: Zero-gate transition bound from residual widths. Let F be a finite binary language of fixed length N, and let L_t be the number of live length-t prefixes. statement: statement: Residual-class counting identity. Let F be a finite binary language of fixed length N and let R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each prefix p of length t. The number of distinct residual classes at layer t is |{R_t(p): R_t(p) is nonempty}| + 1[there exists a dead length-t prefix]. Proof: Every live prefix has a nonempty residual, and distinct nonempty residuals are exactly the nonempty residual classes by definition. Every dead prefix has residual equal to the empty set, so all dead prefixes contribute exactly one additional class if any exist, and none otherwise. These classes are disjoint because the empty set is not nonempty. Scope: all finite fixed-length binary languages and all layers 0<=t<=N. statement: statement: Exact residual-state lower bound and matching construction. Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, and define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F}. Let K_t be the number of distinct residuals R_t(p) over prefixes p of length t. Any deterministic streaming membership machine that must correctly decide acceptance for every remaining suffix has at least K_t distinct states at layer t. If R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, choose a suffix u in their symmetric difference; sharing a state after p and q would force the same answer on u, contradicting correctness. Conversely, use the residual set itself as state. On bit b, transition R to {v: bv is in R}; at the terminal layer accept iff the empty suffix belongs to R. Hence the minimum number of states at layer t is K_t, and the minimum uniform state-bit count is ceil(log2(max_t K_t)), allowing zero bits when max_t K_t=1. This characterizes state capacity only; it gives no per-step circuit-gate bound.

label: S0812
statement: statement: Zero-gate essential-position bound. Let F:{0,1}^N->{0,1} be recognized by a deterministic layered streaming machine with a fixed initial state and S state bits. At each update, every next-state bit is either a constant or a literal (possibly negated) of one current-state bit or of the incoming input bit; fan-out is unrestricted. The terminal decoder is any Boolean function of the final S state bits. If every input position is essential for F, then S>=N. Proof: Induct on t. At t=0 every state bit is constant. If each state bit after t updates is constant or a literal of one of the first t input bits, then each next-state bit, being constant or a literal of an old state bit or the new input bit, is constant or a literal of one of the first t+1 input bits. Thus after N updates each final state bit depends on at most one input position, so the entire final state and its decoder depend on at most S positions. If S<N, some position is absent from every final state bit; changing only that bit leaves the final state and decoded output unchanged, contradicting that the position is essential. Scope: Fixed-length deterministic streaming recognition, the stated zero-gate literal/wire update basis, arbitrary terminal decoder. This does not cover updates with any nontrivial gate and gives no decoder-size bound.

statement: statement: Terminal decoder lemma. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N, and represent its residual classes R_N(p)={u in {epsilon}: pu in F} by injective S-bit codes, where S>=1. statement:
statement: Let t,S be positive integers. In a deterministic layered Boolean machine with S state bits, suppose update i computes each bit using a fan-in-two circuit with at most g_i binary gates, whose only sources are the prior state bits and input x_i. Set P_t=∏_{i=1}^t(g_i+1). Every final state bit depends on at most P_t input positions. If the final state is injective on {0,1}^t, then t≤S P_t.
proof: Define a function's support as the input coordinates whose change can change its value. A connected fan-in-two circuit with g gates has at most g+1 distinct source leaves influencing its output. Thus each bit at update i depends on at most g_i+1 prior-state bits or x_i. Inductively, each selected prior-state bit depends on at most P_{i-1} earlier inputs; including x_i, the union has size at most (g_i+1)P_{i-1}=P_i. Therefore each final bit has support size at most P_t, and the union U of all S final-bit supports has size at most S P_t. If |U|<t, some input coordinate affects no final bit, so flipping it preserves the final state, contradicting injectivity. Hence t≤|U|≤S P_t.
scope: Layered Boolean state machines under the stated per-update circuit model. Does not establish SC live/dead separation or an SC-specific cost trade-off.

statement: Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, and call coordinate i essential if there are two strings differing only at i with exactly one in F. Any deterministic layered recognizer for F with fixed initial state, arbitrary terminal decoder, and updates whose outputs are constants or literals of one prior-state bit or the incoming bit requires at least E(F) state bits, where E(F) is the number of essential coordinates. Proof: Induct on updates. Initially each state bit is constant. At each update, a next-state bit is constant or a literal of one old bit or the incoming bit; by induction it is constant or a literal of one input coordinate. Thus the final state depends on at most S coordinates. If an essential coordinate i is absent from all final bits, flipping i leaves the final state unchanged, so the decoder gives the same membership answer on a pair witnessing essentiality, contradiction. Therefore all E(F) essential coordinates must occur among the S final-bit supports, and S>=E(F). Scope includes arbitrary time-dependent wire/literal transitions, free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out, and arbitrary terminal decoding; it makes no positive-gate claim.

statement:
statement: Support-cover bound for layered updates. Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, fixed initial state, and for every layer each of its S next-state output bits be computed from the current S state bits and one new input bit by a circuit with at most G fan-in-two gates; NOT and constants are free and fan-out is unrestricted. Suppose that at some layer t all 2^t input prefixes are live and the transducer's state map on those prefixes is injective. Then t <= S(G+1)^t. Proof: For a Boolean output of a circuit with g fan-in-two gates, restrict to the ancestor subcircuit of that output and discard unused gates. If it has h gates, its underlying undirected graph is connected to the output. Starting at the output and exposing ancestor gates in reverse topological order, each exposed binary gate has at least one wire already exposed and can introduce at most one new primary input; thus at most h+1 distinct primary inputs reach the output. Since h<=G, each next-state bit depends on at most G+1 current state/input coordinates. By induction on layers, each state bit at layer t depends on at most (G+1)^t of the t input positions: each dependency set at the preceding layer is replaced by the union of at most G+1 such sets, with the new input included as one coordinate. Injectivity on all 2^t prefixes implies every input position affects at least one state bit; otherwise flipping an absent position preserves the state. The union of S support sets therefore covers t positions and has size at most S(G+1)^t, proving the inequality. The finite closure computation cm-8f32be27451948a5 found no counterexample for d<=3 and <=3 AND/XOR gates; it is a sanity check only, not used in the proof.
scope: Finite layered deterministic transducers under the stated fan-in-two update model; conclusion applies only at a full-live layer with injective prefix states. It does not imply a positive G lower bound for SC families or settle Lemma M.

statement: Corrected support-cover bound. statement: Fixed-coordinate prefix representation with explicit dead flag. For every N>=0 and F subseteq {0,1}^N, a layered deterministic recognizer for F can use N+1 state bits: live prefix p at layer t is encoded by (0,p followed by N-t zeroes), and the dead state is (1,0^N). On a live encoding and bit b, transition to the padded code of pb if pb extends to a word in F, and otherwise to dead; dead remains dead. At layer N accept exactly live states. This specifies a correct transition table for every finite F but gives no AND/XOR circuit-size bound for the viability predicate.
proof: Padding is injective on length-t prefixes, and the first coordinate separates dead from live. By definition, pb is live exactly when some word of F has prefix pb. Thus each transition reaches the prescribed child code exactly when that child is live, and otherwise reaches dead. Induction over layers shows that the state is live exactly on prefixes extendible to F; at layer N this is exactly membership in F.
scope: All finite binary languages F subseteq {0,1}^N; N+1 state bits; semantic transition table only.

label: S0820
statement:
statement: Truth-table update bound for the fixed-coordinate prefix recognizer. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N. In the N+1-bit state encoding with padded prefixes and a dead flag, every layer transition can be implemented by a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with free NOTs and constants using at most (N+1)(2^(N+2)(N+1)-1) gates.
proof: Each transition has d=N+2 Boolean inputs (the N+1 state bits and the incoming bit) and q=N+1 Boolean outputs. For each output, write its truth table as an OR of at most 2^d minterms. Each minterm costs at most d-1 fan-in-two AND gates. Combining at most 2^d terms costs at most 2^d-1 gates because OR(a,b)=NOT(AND(NOT(a),NOT(b))) uses one AND gate and free NOTs. Thus each output uses at most 2^d(d-1)+(2^d-1)=2^d d-1 gates; multiplying by q yields (N+1)(2^(N+2)(N+1)-1). This applies to any total extension of the specified reachable-state transition map.
scope: All F subseteq {0,1}^N; fixed-coordinate padded-prefix state; fan-in-two AND/XOR basis, free NOTs/constants; no claim of optimality.

label: S0821
statement:
statement: One-hot residual transition construction. Let F be any finite binary language of fixed length N. At layer t, let R_t be the distinct nonempty residual languages after prefixes of length t, and let k_t=|R_t|. Use one-hot indicators for each residual and one additional dead indicator. For each transition layer, a deterministic recognizer exists whose next-state bits are computed by ORs of terms x_r AND [b=a], with one term per labeled arc from a live residual r on bit a to a nonempty child residual. Include dead-to-dead arcs. If E_t is the number of such arcs, the total number of fan-in-two AND/OR gates is at most 2E_t; OR is implementable in the allowed AND/NOT basis with free NOTs. The state width is k_t+1 bits.
proof: For each residual r and input bit a, define the derivative r_a={v:av is in r}. This derivative is either empty, in which case the next state is dead, or a unique member of R_{t+1}. For each next residual r', set its indicator to the OR of x_r AND [b=a] over exactly the arcs whose derivative is r'. Each arc uses at most one AND; combining all arc terms for each output uses at most the number of terms minus one OR gates, so across live outputs the cost is at most 2E_t. The dead indicator is handled by including every arc with empty derivative and the dead self-loops among the arcs; the same bound applies to its OR. Starting from the one-hot state for F, induction on t shows that after reading prefix p the represented residual is {v:pv in F}; at t=N this accepts exactly when the empty suffix belongs to that residual, equivalently p is in F.
scope: All finite binary languages F of length N; layered residual automata; one-hot states including dead; AND/OR fan-in two with free NOT and constants. This gives a width/update tradeoff and does not bound G_max at the assigned minimum binary width.

label: S0822
statement:
statement: Zero-gate SEARCH width bound. In a deterministic layered transducer with S state bits, zero fan-in-two gates per update, and free wires, constants, and unrestricted fan-out, if the state after t updates is injective on all 2^t binary prefixes, then S >= t.
proof: With zero fan-in-two gates, each next-state coordinate is a wire from a previous state coordinate, the current input, or a constant. Inductively each coordinate after t updates is either constant or a copy of one of the t input bits. Hence at most S input positions affect the final state. If S<t, an input position affects no coordinate, so flipping it preserves the state, contradicting injectivity on all 2^t prefixes.
scope: All integers S>=0,t>=1; deterministic layered binary transducers; zero fan-in-two gates per update; wires/constants free; full SEARCH injectivity on every length-t prefix. Does not bound decoder cost or positive gate counts.

label: S0823
statement:
statement: Zero-gate support bound (exact finite transducer model). Fix integers S>=1 and t>=1. Consider a deterministic layered binary transducer with a fixed initial state in {0,1}^S. At each update, each next-state coordinate is a constant, a state-bit wire, or the current input-bit wire; free NOT gates may complement any such wire. Then each state coordinate after t updates is a constant or a literal of one of the t input bits. Consequently, if the final state is injective on all 2^t length-t inputs, then S>=t.
Proof: Induct on update layers. Initially each coordinate is constant. If each coordinate before a layer is constant or an input literal, then a next coordinate that is constant, a current state wire (possibly complemented), or the new input wire (possibly complemented) is again constant or an input literal. Thus after t layers every coordinate depends on at most one input position. Across S coordinates at most S positions occur. If S<t, one input position occurs in no coordinate; flipping that position leaves the final state unchanged, contradicting injectivity.
scope: All S>=1,t>=1; fixed initial state; zero fan-in-two gates; free NOTs, constants, and wires; full SEARCH injectivity on all length-t prefixes. Does not address positive gate counts, arbitrary dead/live semantics, decoder cost, or the Lemma M Pareto objective.

label: S0824
statement:
statement: Essential-coordinate lower bound for zero-gate membership machines. Let F be a Boolean function on {0,1}^N computed by a deterministic layered transducer with a fixed initial state of S bits. At every update, each state coordinate is a constant, a state-bit wire, or the current input bit, optionally complemented; the final output is an arbitrary Boolean function of the final state. If F depends essentially on k input coordinates, then S >= k.
proof: Induct on the update layers. Initially every state coordinate is constant. A zero-gate update copies or complements one previous state coordinate, copies or complements the current input bit, or outputs a constant. Thus after all N updates each state coordinate is constant or a literal of one input coordinate. The final output, being a function only of these S coordinates, is independent of every input coordinate absent from their combined support. Hence all k essential coordinates must occur among at most S supported coordinates, and S >= k.
scope: All finite N and S; fixed initial state; zero fan-in-two gates per update; free NOTs and constants; arbitrary terminal decoder; exact membership computation on every input.

label: S0825
statement:
statement: Nonuniform layerwise support bound. Let a deterministic layered transducer have S state bits, fixed initial state, and update i computed by a fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with g_i gates, free NOTs/constants, and unrestricted fan-out. Define r_0=0 and r_i=(g_i+1)r_{i-1}+1. After i updates, each state coordinate depends on at most r_i input positions. Consequently, if the final state distinguishes every input in a set A subseteq {0,1}^i from every input in a disjoint set B (in particular, if it computes a Boolean function f exactly), then the union of essential input coordinates of f has size at most S r_i.
proof: Induct on i. At i=0 every state coordinate is fixed and has empty input support, so the bound r_0=0 holds. At update i, prune the circuit for one next-state coordinate to its ancestors. In a fan-in-two circuit with g_i gates, the output depends on at most g_i+1 distinct primary inputs: the output ancestor graph is connected, and each binary gate can add at most one new leaf. The primary inputs are the S previous state bits and the current input bit. Hence the next coordinate depends on at most g_i+1 previous state coordinates and possibly the current bit; by the induction hypothesis its support among earlier inputs has size at most (g_i+1)r_{i-1}, and adding the current bit gives at most (g_i+1)r_{i-1}+1=r_i. Taking the union over S final coordinates gives at most S r_i input positions on which the final state depends. Any input coordinate outside this union leaves the final state unchanged under a flip, so an exactly computed Boolean function cannot be essential in that coordinate. Thus its number of essential coordinates is at most S r_i.
scope: Finite deterministic layered transducers; fixed initial state; layer i has g_i fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out; arbitrary final decoder. The distinction conclusion applies to Boolean functions computed exactly on all inputs; for set separation it bounds coordinates on which final-state equality can vary, not arbitrary pairwise separations.

label: S0826
statement:
statement: Leaf-budget support recurrence. Fix a deterministic layered transducer with S state bits and fixed initial state. Update i is an acyclic fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with g_i gates, free NOTs/constants and unrestricted fan-out, on the S old state bits and current input bit x_i. Let r_0=0 and r_i=max{ min(S,g_i+1) r_{i-1}, min(S,g_i) r_{i-1}+1 }. After i updates each state coordinate depends on at most r_i input positions. Thus an exactly computed Boolean function on the i-bit streams has at most S r_i essential coordinates.
proof: Induct on i. At i=0 each state coordinate is constant. For a given next-state output, retain only its ancestor circuit. A binary-gate DAG with g_i gates has at most g_i+1 distinct primary input leaves: starting from the output and traversing ancestors, each binary gate can introduce at most one additional leaf, and sharing/repeated inputs cannot increase the number. Let b be the number of distinct old-state-bit leaves and c the indicator that x_i is a leaf. Then b+c<=g_i+1 and b<=S. By induction, the output support among x_1,...,x_{i-1} is at most b r_{i-1}; its support can additionally include x_i only if c=1. If c=0, this is at most min(S,g_i+1)r_{i-1}; if c=1, b<=min(S,g_i), giving at most min(S,g_i)r_{i-1}+1. Hence it is bounded by r_i. Unioning the supports of S final coordinates gives at most S r_i positions; a coordinate outside this union cannot affect the final state and therefore cannot be essential for any terminal Boolean decoder.
scope: Finite deterministic layered transducers; each update is an acyclic fan-in-two AND/XOR circuit with g_i gates over old state bits and the current stream bit; free NOTs/constants, unrestricted fan-out; fixed initial state and arbitrary terminal decoder. This is a support upper bound only, not a positive-gate lower bound for SC membership.

label: S0827
statement:
statement: Zero-gate full-layer characterization. Fix integers t>=1 and S>=1. Consider a deterministic layered transducer initialized in a fixed state, with S state bits and zero counted fan-in-two update gates; NOTs and constants are free. If all 2^t length-t input strings must reach pairwise distinct states, then S>=t. Conversely, for every S>=t there is such a zero-gate transducer whose states after t updates are pairwise distinct on all 2^t strings. Proof: With zero gates, each next-state coordinate is a constant, a copy of one old state coordinate, its negation, the current input bit, or its negation: without gates, the only available wires are circuit inputs. Inductively, after t updates each coordinate is a constant or a literal of at most one of the t input positions. If some position occurs in no coordinate, flipping it leaves the whole state unchanged, contradicting pairwise distinctness. Thus every one of t positions must occur in the S coordinates, so S>=t. Conversely, use t coordinates as a shift register: at update j (1<=j<=t), write the new input into coordinate j and leave coordinates 1,...,j-1 unchanged; any extra coordinates remain constant. This uses only wires and constants, and after t updates the first t coordinates equal the complete input word, so all 2^t states are distinct. Scope: Injectivity on one full layer only; it neither enforces an additional dead code nor gives a bound for positive gate count or any particular SC family.
scope: All finite t>=1 and S>=1 in the stated zero-gate layered transducer model; injectivity is required only among all length-t input prefixes.

label: S0828
statement:
statement: Residual distinguishability lower bound for layered streaming machines. Let F be a nonempty subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=t<=N, define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu is in F}, for every prefix p of length t, and let K_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p). Any deterministic layered membership machine that recognizes F exactly must have at least K_t distinct states at layer t. If it has S_t binary state bits, then S_t >= ceil(log2 K_t). If the layer also contains a dead prefix whose state must differ from all live-prefix states, replace K_t by K_t+1 when there is at least one dead prefix. Proof: Suppose p and q have different residual sets. There is a suffix u in their symmetric difference. Without loss, pu is in F and qu is not. If p and q reached the same state at layer t, determinism implies that reading the same remaining suffix u from that state has the same outcome in both runs, contradicting exact recognition. Therefore prefixes from distinct residual classes occupy distinct states. With K_t such classes, the state set has size at least K_t, hence 2^{S_t}>=K_t and S_t>=ceil(log2 K_t). In the dead-prefix variant, a dead state cannot coincide with any live residual state: choose a suffix completing that live prefix to F; the dead prefix followed by that suffix must reject, while the live one accepts. Thus it requires one additional state. This lower bound matches the residual-class construction’s state count at each layer, but says nothing about update-gate count or decoder cost.
scope: Every finite binary language F of fixed length N and every deterministic layered exact membership machine. The extra dead-state clause applies when the machine’s specification requires a dead prefix to have a state distinct from all live-prefix states.

label: S0829
statement: statement: Correct live/dead state lower bound. Fix a finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N and a layer t. Let L be the set of prefixes designated live, and suppose every p in L has a nonempty residual R_t(p)={u:pu in F}. Let K be the number of distinct residuals among prefixes in L. Any deterministic exact machine that must represent every live prefix and at least one dead prefix at this layer in distinct live/dead categories needs at least K+1 states. Proof: For each two live prefixes with different residuals, some suffix belongs to exactly one residual; if their states were equal, determinism would give the same acceptance outcome after that suffix, a contradiction. Thus the K live residual classes require K distinct states. A dead prefix cannot share a state with any live prefix: each live prefix has an accepting suffix, while every suffix from a dead prefix must reject. Therefore one further state is required. Scope: the designated live prefixes have nonempty residuals, and dead means no accepting completion. This corrects the ambiguity in counting dead prefixes among all residual classes; it gives a state lower bound, not a gate lower bound.

A dead prefix cannot share a state with any live prefix: each live prefix has an accepting suffix, while every suffix from a dead prefix must reject. Therefore one further state is required. Scope: the designated live prefixes have nonempty residuals, and dead means no accepting completion. This corrects the ambiguity in counting dead prefixes among all residual classes; it gives a state lower bound, not a gate lower bound.

label: S0830
statement: statement: Sparse-transition circuit upper bound. Let a deterministic layered machine have S state bits and one input bit per update, and suppose its prescribed next-state map is defined on r distinct reachable state/input pairs. With fan-in-two AND gates, free NOTs and constants, and unrestricted fan-out, that map on the reachable pairs can be extended to all inputs and implemented with at most S*r*(S+r) gates. Proof: For each prescribed pair a in {0,1}^{S+1}, form its equality indicator I_a as the conjunction of its S+1 matching literals. A binary AND tree uses S gates; literals and their negations are free. For each output coordinate j, OR the indicators whose prescribed output bit is 1, using at most r-1 fan-in-two AND gates via De Morgan and free NOTs (the empty OR is constant 0). On each prescribed pair exactly its own indicator is 1, so every output coordinate is correct there. The total is at most r*S + S*(r-1), which is at most S*r*(S+r). This gives a constructive update-circuit bound parameterized by reachable transition count; it can improve on full truth-table synthesis when r is small. Scope: any finite partial deterministic update map on r distinct inputs of width S+1, with the stated gate basis; no claim is made about optimality or decoder cost.

label: S0831
statement:
statement: Zero-gate layered update characterization. Fix t>=0 and S>=1. Consider a deterministic layered transducer with fixed initial state in {0,1}^S; at each step i, each of the S output coordinates is selected from constants 0,1, the S current-state coordinates, or the newly arriving bit x_i, with arbitrary fan-out and optional negation, and no fan-in-2 gates. Then after t steps every state coordinate is either a constant or a literal x_j or ¬x_j for some j in {1,...,t}. Consequently the final state depends on at most S of the t input positions.
proof: Induct on t. At t=0 every state coordinate is constant by the fixed initial-state assumption. Suppose the assertion holds after t steps. At step t+1, an output coordinate is either constant, the new input x_{t+1} or its negation, or a current-state coordinate or its negation. By the induction hypothesis, the latter is constant or a literal of some x_j with j≤t; negating it preserves that form. Thus every coordinate has the asserted form after t+1. The final S coordinates mention at most S distinct input positions, so changing any other position while holding the mentioned bits fixed leaves the final state unchanged.

label: S0832
statement:
statement: Sharpened bounded-gate support lemma. Let S>=1 and G>=1. In a layered transducer with fixed initial state and at most G fan-in-two gates per update, free NOTs/constants, and unrestricted fan-out, after t updates each state coordinate depends on at most ((G+1)^t-1)/G input positions. Hence, if every prefix on a layer of length t is live and distinct live prefixes must have distinct states, then t <= S((G+1)^t-1)/G. For G=0, each state coordinate is constant or a signed copy of one input bit, so the total final state depends on at most S positions.
proof: Let a_t bound the number of input positions in the support of any one state coordinate after t updates. Initially a_0=0. In one update, an output coordinate computed with at most G binary gates depends on at most G+1 distinct primary inputs, since its connected ancestor circuit with G gates has at most G+1 leaves. Those primary inputs are selected among the S previous state coordinates and the arriving bit. Thus its support after substitution is contained in the union of at most G+1 prior state-coordinate supports and possibly the arriving input; a safe recurrence is a_{t+1} <= (G+1)a_t+1. Solving from a_0=0 gives a_t <= ((G+1)^t-1)/G. Across S coordinates the full state depends on at most S a_t positions. If this is less than t, some position is absent from all coordinates, so flipping it preserves the state, contradicting distinct states for all 2^t live prefixes; therefore the displayed necessary inequality holds. When G=0 each output is a constant or signed copy of one of the prior coordinates or arriving bit; induction shows each coordinate is constant or a signed copy of one input position, giving at most S positions total.

label: S0833
statement: statement: Residual-state lower bound for exact layered membership machines. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and for 0<=t<=N define R_t(p)={u in {0,1}^{N-t}: pu in F} for each p in {0,1}^t. Any deterministic layered machine that reads the N input bits in order, starts from a fixed state, and accepts exactly F must have at least K_t distinct states at layer t, where K_t is the number of distinct residual sets R_t(p), including the empty residual if it occurs. Proof: Suppose p,q are length-t prefixes with R_t(p) != R_t(q). Their symmetric difference is nonempty, so choose suffix u in R_t(p) triangle R_t(q). If the machine had the same layer-t state after p and q, determinism implies its state and final acceptance after the common continuation u are identical. But exactly one of pu,qu belongs to F by the choice of u, contradicting exact recognition. Thus prefixes with distinct residuals reach distinct layer-t states, and there are K_t such residual classes. Scope: Every finite binary language F of fixed length N; deterministic, exact, one-pass, ordered layered membership machines; no restriction on transition computation. This lower bound is information-theoretic only and gives no transition-gate lower bound.

label: S0834
statement:
statement: Zero-gate full-layer injectivity lemma. Let S>=1 and t>=1. In a layered deterministic transducer with fixed initial state, S state bits, and zero counted fan-in-two update gates (free NOTs and constants; wires allowed), the states after t updates can be injective on all 2^t length-t input prefixes if and only if S>=t.
Proof. For sufficiency when S>=t, store the prefix in the first t coordinates. At update i (1<=i<=t), copy the new input bit into coordinate i and carry each earlier stored bit from coordinate j to j. The remaining coordinates may be constants. This uses only wires and therefore zero counted gates; after t steps the state contains the full prefix.
For necessity, with zero gates each next-state coordinate is a constant or a literal of one previous state coordinate or of the current input bit. By induction on updates, each state coordinate after t steps is a constant or a literal of at most one of the t input positions: constants remain constant, and wiring selects one existing coordinate or the new input, with optional negation. If t>S, at least one of the t input positions occurs in no state coordinate. Two prefixes differing only at that position then produce the same state, so the map is not injective. Hence injectivity requires S>=t.
Scope: This is SEARCH injectivity on a full layer in the stated zero-gate update model; it does not establish live/dead separation, decoder cost, or an optimal (S,G_max,D) Pareto point for SC families.

A corrected exhaustive existence check has been requested separately.

label: S0835
statement:
statement: Sparse reachable-row transition construction. Let d>=1, q>=1, and let P be a partially specified q-output Boolean map on {0,1}^d with exactly r specified input rows. There is a total extension of P whose q outputs are computable using at most 2^(d+1)-4 + q max(0,r-1) fan-in-two AND/XOR gates, with NOTs/constants free and fan-out unrestricted. Proof: Set every unspecified output bit to 0. Build every d-bit minterm using the shared prefix tree: the length-1 literals are free, and for each prefix of length j>=2 AND its length-(j-1) prefix minterm with the next literal. This uses sum_{j=2}^d 2^j = 2^(d+1)-4 AND gates. For each output, XOR the minterms corresponding to specified rows on which that output is 1; there are at most r such terms and hence at most max(0,r-1) XOR gates. The minterms are mutually exclusive, so this realizes the selected truth table exactly, and all unspecified rows output zero. Scope: arbitrary partial Boolean transition maps under the stated basis; no claim of optimality.
scope: All finite partial multi-output Boolean maps with d input bits and q output bits.

structure.evidence: Constructive argument: shared prefix minterm tree has exactly sum_{j=2}^d 2^j gates; the zero extension has at most r one-rows per output, and XOR of k mutually exclusive minterms realizes their indicator union using k-1 gates for k>0. This provides a layerwise upper bound when fewer than 2^d transition rows are reachable. It does not settle joint encoding minimization for SC_{3,1}.
structure.gap: This layerwise construction can shrink the implementation ceiling on sparse layers, but the open S=4 exact G_max synthesis still requires optimizing encodings and shared transition logic across all layers.

label: S0836
statement:
statement: Zero-gate support theorem for arbitrary terminal decoders. Let N,S>=0. Consider a deterministic layered transducer with S state bits, a fixed initial state, and updates whose outputs are constants, wires, or negated wires, with no fan-in-two gates. For every t<=N, each state coordinate after t updates is either constant or equal to one input coordinate x_i or its negation; hence the entire state depends on at most S input coordinates. Consequently, if the machine's terminal output is D(q_N) for an arbitrary Boolean decoder D and computes a Boolean function f on {0,1}^N, then f depends on at most S input coordinates. Proof: Induct on t. At t=0 every coordinate is fixed and thus constant. In an update, each output is a constant or a literal of one prior state coordinate or of the new input bit. Substituting the induction hypothesis shows each new coordinate is constant or a literal of a single input coordinate. At t=N, let I be the union of input indices occurring in the S coordinates, so |I|<=S. The decoder output is a function only of q_N, hence only of x restricted to I. If two inputs agree on I, they produce the same q_N and same decoder output; therefore every coordinate outside I is inessential for f. This argument permits arbitrary terminal decoding and time-dependent updates.
scope: All finite lengths N and state widths S in deterministic layered transducers with zero counted fan-in-two update gates; free constants, wires and NOT; unrestricted terminal decoder. It constrains recognition support, not witness output, decoder cost, or positive gate counts.

label: S0837
statement:
statement: For a finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N and cut t in {0,...,N}, let R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F} for each length-t prefix p, and let r_t be the number of distinct sets R_t(p), including the empty set if it occurs. The minimum number of states at layer t among deterministic one-pass recognizers of F is exactly r_t.
proof: Upper bound: assign each length-t prefix p the state R_t(p). On reading bit b, update residual R to R'={z in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bz in R}. If R=R_t(p), then z is in R' iff bz is in R_t(p), iff p(bz) is in F, iff (pb)z is in F. Thus R'=R_{t+1}(pb), so the transition is well-defined from the residual state. At t=N, the residual is {epsilon} for accepted words and empty for rejected words; accept exactly in state {epsilon}. This constructs a recognizer with r_t states at each layer. For the lower bound, distinct residuals R_t(p), R_t(q) have a suffix z in their symmetric difference. Exactly one of pz,qz belongs to F. If p and q reached the same state, determinism would force the same final state after z and therefore the same decision, a contradiction. Hence distinct residuals require distinct states, proving equality.
scope: Exact state count for deterministic layered one-pass recognizers with fixed input order, one transition per input bit, and final accept/reject depending only on final state. This gives no transition-circuit or decoder gate-cost bound.

label: S0838
statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix 0<=t<=N. For each length-t prefix p define R_t(p)={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: pz in F}. In every deterministic layered recognizer of F, distinct sets R_t(p) require distinct states at layer t; conversely, there is a deterministic layered recognizer with exactly one reachable state per distinct R_t(p) at each layer. Thus the minimum reachable width at layer t, without transition-cost restrictions, is |{R_t(p): |p|=t}|. Proof: If R_t(p) and R_t(q) differ, choose z in their symmetric difference; exactly one of pz,qz belongs to F, so the recognizer must be in different states after p and q, since a shared state followed by z has identical future transitions and acceptance. For the converse, use the distinct residual sets as layer-t states. From R_t(p), on bit b transition to R_{t+1}(pb); this is well-defined because equal residual sets have equal derivatives: z is in R_{t+1}(pb) iff bz is in R_t(p). At layer N accept iff the residual contains the empty word. Starting at R_0(empty) yields the correct recognition of F, and every state included is reachable by a prefix that defines it. This construction imposes no bound on the Boolean circuit size of a transition.

label: S0839
statement:
statement: Let q>=2 and k=ceil(log2 q). For any deterministic transition map delta: Q x {0,1}->Q on a set Q of q states, there is a fan-in-2 Boolean circuit with k output bits that agrees with the binary encoding of delta on every valid encoded state and both input bits, using at most q(k-1)+2k(q-1)+3k gates; the circuit may be arbitrary on unused encodings.
proof: Fix an injective encoding c:Q->{0,1}^k. For each u in Q, form the equality indicator e_u(x)=1 iff x=c(u), using a binary AND tree with k-1 gates; complemented input literals are treated as free wires. For each input symbol b and output coordinate i, form y_{b,i}=OR_{u: c(delta(u,b))_i=1} e_u, using at most q-1 OR gates (an empty OR is constant 0). The indicators are shared across all outputs. Select y_{0,i} or y_{1,i} using the input bit b with two AND gates and one OR gate, for 3k gates total. On valid encoding c(u), exactly e_u is 1, so y_{b,i}=c(delta(u,b))_i and the mux returns the correct next-state bit. Summing gives q(k-1)+2k(q-1)+3k. If NOT gates are charged, add at most k shared input-inverter gates.
scope: Finite deterministic layered machines with q>=2 states, binary input, fixed injective k-bit state encoding; fan-in-2 AND/OR gates and complemented input literals treated as free wires. If NOT gates are charged, add at most k shared input-inverter gates.

label: S0841
statement:
statement: For every integer N>=1 and every finite search problem on inputs x in {0,1}^N with a specified output y(x) for each accepted x, there is a deterministic layered streaming transducer with N state bits, zero Boolean update gates, and a final-state decoder that outputs y(x) on accepted inputs and rejects the others.
proof: At layer t, store the t bits read so far in state coordinates 1 through t and set the remaining coordinates to zero. Initially the state is all zero. The transition from layer t to t+1 copies coordinates 1 through t unchanged, wires the newly read input bit into coordinate t+1, and sets all later coordinates to zero. These are constants and direct wires, so the transition uses no Boolean gates. Inductively, after t symbols the state is (x_1,...,x_t,0,...,0). After N symbols the state is exactly x. Define the final decoder on each state x to return y(x) if x is accepted and reject otherwise. This decoder is well-defined because distinct complete inputs have distinct final states.
scope: Layer-dependent transitions, N state bits, unrestricted deterministic final decoder, and zero cost for constants and direct wires. The result gives no bound when decoder complexity or transition uniformity is restricted; it does not imply an SC-specific lower bound.

proof: At layer t, store the t bits read so far in state coordinates 1 through t and set the remaining coordinates to zero. Initially the state is all zero. The transition from layer t to t+1 copies coordinates 1 through t unchanged, wires the newly read input bit into coordinate t+1, and sets all later coordinates to zero. These are constants and direct wires, so the transition uses no Boolean gates. Inductively, after t symbols the state is (x_1,...,x_t,0,...,0). After N symbols the state is exactly x. Define the final decoder on each state x to return y(x) if x is accepted and reject otherwise. This decoder is well-defined because distinct complete inputs have distinct final states.
scope: Layer-dependent transitions, N state bits, unrestricted deterministic final decoder, and zero cost for constants and direct wires. The result gives no bound when decoder complexity or transition uniformity is restricted; it does not imply an SC-specific lower bound.

label: S0842
statement:
statement: For every finite binary language F subseteq {0,1}^N, there is a deterministic layered transducer with N state bits that, after t input bits, stores those t bits in the first t state positions and zeros in the remaining positions, using zero non-constant gates per update. At each layer, its state is injective on all length-t prefixes, so it separates every live prefix from every dead prefix. A final-state decoder can decide membership in F and, for accepted inputs, output any fixed valid witness associated with that input.
proof: Let q_0=0^N. At layer t<N define F_t(q,b)=(q_1,...,q_t,b,0,...,0), using the known layer index t; each output is a wire from a state coordinate, the current input, or constant zero, so the update uses no non-constant gates. Inductively, after prefix p of length t the state is p followed by N-t zeros. Distinct length-t prefixes therefore have distinct states. A dead prefix and a live prefix are distinct words of the same length, so their states differ. At the final layer the state is the full input word, and a decoder can determine membership in the finite set F and return the corresponding fixed witness on members. This establishes correctness of the transducer and the zero update-gate bound; it makes no claim about decoder size.
scope: All finite F subseteq {0,1}^N; state width S=N; time-dependent layered updates; B2 basis includes wires and constants; final decoder unrestricted. The claim is not an update-cost bound for S<N and does not bound decoder cost.

label: S0843
statement:
statement: For any finite layered deterministic transducer whose layer-t states are encoded by S bits, the prescribed next-state map on reachable (state,input-bit) pairs can be implemented by a multi-output circuit over AND, XOR, NOT, and constants with at most (S+1)+S*2^(S+1)*(S+1) nonconstant gates. Proof: Put d=S+1. For each output bit, extend its prescribed values arbitrarily to all 2^d inputs. Express the extended function as a DNF with at most 2^d minterms. Share the input literals and their negations across outputs, using at most d NOT gates. Each minterm uses at most d-1 AND gates; combining at most 2^d terms by De Morgan uses at most 2^d additional AND/NOT gates. Thus each output uses at most d*2^d gates, plus at most d shared negations overall. This implements every prescribed transition; unreachable inputs are unconstrained. This is a universal finite upper bound only and gives no lower bound or exact minimum G_max for SC_{n,s}.
scope: All S>=0 and finite layered deterministic transitions with one input bit and S-bit state; AND, XOR, NOT, constants; count nonconstant gates, fan-out free.

label: S0844
statement:
statement: Let F be a nonempty finite set of accepted length-N streams, and let P_t={p in {0,1}^t: p is a prefix of some f in F}, L_t=|P_t|, and let d_t be 1 if some length-t prefix is not in P_t and 0 otherwise. In the full-search model, in which distinct live prefixes at layer t must occupy distinct states and a dead prefix must occupy a state disjoint from all live-prefix states, every layer-t state space has size at least L_t+d_t; hence an S-bit machine must satisfy 2^S >= L_t+d_t. Proof: The L_t live prefixes inject into layer-t states by the model's full-search requirement, so their image has size L_t. If d_t=1, take a dead prefix r. Its state is required to be outside that image by dead/live separation, adding at least one state. If d_t=0 there is no additional state requirement. Therefore the number of layer-t states is at least L_t+d_t. Since S bits encode at most 2^S states, the inequality follows. The bound is sharp as a pure counting bound: assigning distinct codes to the L_t live prefixes and, when needed, one further code to a dead prefix uses exactly L_t+d_t codes; this does not assert that transitions or a final decoder can be implemented within any gate/size budget.
scope: Every finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N, every 0<=t<=N, full-search layered deterministic machines under the binding requirement that live prefixes are pairwise state-distinct and dead prefixes have codes disjoint from live codes. This establishes only state capacity, not transition cost G_max or decoder cost D.

label: S0845
statement:
statement: For any finite language F subseteq {0,1}^N under the binding full-search semantics, there is a layered deterministic transducer that uses exactly L_t + d_t states at each layer t, where P_t is the set of length-t prefixes of members of F, L_t=|P_t|, and d_t=1 iff some length-t string is outside P_t. Thus its maximum layer width is max_t (L_t+d_t).
scope: Finite binary languages; state width only. No bound on update gates G_max or decoder cost D.
proof: At layer t, assign one distinct state to each p in P_t and, if d_t=1, one additional state ⊥_t for all non-live prefixes. On input bit b, the state for p transitions to the state for pb when pb is live, and otherwise to ⊥_{t+1}; ⊥_t transitions to ⊥_{t+1}. At the final layer, the live states are exactly the accepted words, and the dead state, when present, is rejecting. A final decoder can associate each live word-state with its required search witness. The construction uses exactly L_t+d_t states at layer t. Conversely, the binding semantics require L_t distinct live states and a separate dead state when one exists, so no machine in this model can use fewer at that layer. This establishes an exact state-width optimum, not an update-circuit or decoder optimum.

label: S0846
statement:
statement: For any deterministic layered transducer update F_t:{0,1}^S×{0,1}->{0,1}^S, each output coordinate has an exact DNF with at most 2^(S+1) minterms, and hence an AND/NOT implementation with at most (S+1)2^(S+1) AND gates plus 2^(S+1) NOT gates per coordinate (OR is implemented by De Morgan). Thus the whole update has at most S((S+1)2^(S+1)+2^(S+1)) nonconstant gates; this also implements any prescribed reachable transitions because unreachable inputs can be assigned arbitrarily.
proof: Fix an output coordinate j. For each input u=(q,b) in {0,1}^{S+1} with F_t(u)_j=1, form the minterm M_u=AND_{k=1}^{S+1} l_{u,k}, where l_{u,k} is input k if u_k=1 and its negation otherwise. The disjunction of these minterms evaluates to 1 exactly on the inputs whose jth output bit is 1, so it equals F_t(·)_j on the entire domain. Each minterm uses at most S AND gates after its literals are available; counting literals conservatively gives at most S+1 AND gates per minterm. Negating each input uses at most S+1 NOT gates, shared across all minterms and outputs (the displayed bound conservatively charges them per output). Implement the disjunction by De Morgan using NOT and AND; charging at most one additional NOT per minterm yields the stated conservative per-output count. Summing over S outputs gives the claimed bound. Since the target transition is specified only on reachable code/bit pairs, extend it arbitrarily to the remaining Boolean inputs and apply the construction.
scope: All S>=1 and all finite deterministic one-bit layered updates with S-bit states; basis AND, NOT, constants, fan-out free. A coarse constructive upper bound only; it gives no lower bound or minimum G_max and does not establish the required fixed-(S,D) Pareto point for SC_{n,s}.
evidence: Pending independent finite verification of the minterm realization via the requested code_run; proof is by direct truth-table construction.
